    The orgs server has slide exporters too: revealjs, and depending on its configuration impressjs, deckjs, webslides and others, each with its own themes. Org: orgs Export File lists them; the deck is written as file.revealjs.html (and so on), so it does not replace an html export. The orgs web ui can also present a file (Presentation in Org: orgs Open Web UI). See the orgs Server section.

    orgs Server

    What the orgs server adds beyond the agenda and capture: query search, habits, clock reports, full text search and more.

    What the Server Adds

    The orgs server

    Everything in OrgEverywhere that looks across files - the agenda, capture, refile, clocking, ids, backlinks - goes through the orgs server. The server also brings features OrgEverywhere never had. They are in the command palette as Org: orgs …, need a connected server, and are shared with worg, the orgs command line and VSCode.

    Most of them open either a quick panel (with a preview of each heading as you move, orgsPreviewOnHighlight) or a result view. In a result view (habits, clock report, text search results) enter or a double click opens the line's heading and g (Org: orgs Refresh Result View) rebuilds the view.

    Finding things

    Query search

    Org: orgs Query Search offers "New query…", your saved queries and the server's filters, then lists the matching headings. A query is an expression such as IsTodo() && HasTags("work") (see The Query Language).

    • Org: orgs Save Query saves a query on the server under a name. Saved queries are yours, and show up in worg and the command line too.
    • Org: orgs Delete Saved Query removes one.
    • Org: Agenda Query (orgs) shows a query's headings as an agenda list instead (see The Agenda).
    Full text search

    A regular expression search through the text of every org file:

    Command Results
    Org: orgs Full Text Search a quick panel of file, line: text
    Org: orgs Full Text Search (results view) a find results style view
    Org: orgs Full Text Search in This File this file only

    It starts with the word at the cursor. orgsTextSearchIgnoreCase (true) and orgsTextSearchMax (200 matches kept per file) control it.

    Habits

    A habit is a repeating todo with :STYLE: habit:

    * TODO Go for a run
  SCHEDULED: <2026-10-11 Sun .+2d>
  :PROPERTIES:
  :STYLE:    habit
  :END:

    Org: orgs Habits shows every habit over the last orgsHabitDays days (21): whether it is due or late today, the current and best streak, how often it was kept, and a bar with a mark per day (■ done, × missed, · nothing due). In the view t (Org: orgs Toggle Habit Done Today) marks the habit on the line done for today, or takes today's tick back.

    Clock report

    Org: orgs Clock Report sums the clocked time of every file for a period: today, yesterday, this or last week, month or year, or everything. See Clocking.

    File history

    For files in a git repository, Org: orgs File History lists the working copy, the staged index and the commits that touched the file (orgsHistoryLimit, 100). Picking one shows the file as it was then, in a scratch view.

    Contacts, records and birthdays

    The server keeps records: headings with a RECORD property (a contact, a piece of equipment…) filed in collections.

    • Org: orgs Contacts searches your contacts (name, numbers, addresses, notes; empty lists them all) and opens the one you pick.
    • Org: orgs Records asks which collection first, then searches it.
    • Org: orgs Upcoming Birthdays lists birthdays and anniversaries in the next orgsBirthdayDays days (60), with the age.

    The web UI

    Org: orgs Open Web UI opens worg, the server's web interface, in your browser on the app you pick: agenda, search, saved queries, kanban, gantt chart, column view, clock report, tables, files, links, mind map, collections, contacts, code, flashcards, diff and history, presentation, voice notes, starmap. orgsWebUrl sets its address when it is not the server's url. worg asks for its own login.

    Encryption

    The server encrypts heading bodies in org-crypt's format with gpg (when its encryption is set up).

    • Org: orgs Encrypt Heading encrypts the body of the heading at the cursor. With a passphrase (not a key) it asks for it twice.
    • Org: orgs Decrypt Heading either shows the text in a panel (the file stays encrypted; the panel is cleared when you close it, and nothing is saved) or writes it back into the file in the clear.

    Attachments

    Org: orgs Attachments lists the files attached to the heading at the cursor (its attachment folder, from its :ID: or :DIR:). Picking one downloads it to a private temporary folder and opens it: org and text files in Sublime, anything else in its own program.

    Flashcards

    Org: orgs Drill Flashcards reviews org-drill cards: pick a deck the server has, or "Query…" to use the headings a query finds (orgsDrillQuery, HasTags("drill")). Each due card is shown in an Org Drill view with its answer hidden; show the answer, grade yourself 0 to 5, and the server schedules the card's next review. A failed card comes back in the same session.

    New files from templates

    Org: orgs New File from Template asks for one of the server's org directories, a file name, a title and one of the server's file templates, has the server create the file and opens it.

    Updater plugins

    The server's updater plugins change a heading from another system: the jira updater, for one, fills a heading in from its jira issue. Org: orgs Update Heading (Jira/plugin) asks which updater (orgsDefaultUpdater, jira) and runs it on the heading at the cursor. The updater has to be configured on the server.

    Exporting, tangling, dynamic blocks and source blocks

    The server can do some of the work on the file you are editing. Each of these saves the buffer first and waits for the server to read it; what the server writes back reloads into the buffer.

    • Org: orgs Export File exports with any of the server's exporters (html, latex, reveal.js, mermaid…), Org: orgs Export File as PDF straight to pdf. See the exporting guides.
    • Org: orgs Tangle File writes the file's :tangle source blocks out.
    • Org: orgs Update Dynamic Blocks refreshes every dynamic block in the file (clocktable, columnview…); Org: orgs Update Dynamic Block at Cursor only the one you are in.
    • Org: orgs Execute Source Block and Org: orgs Execute All Source Blocks run source blocks (and #+CALL: lines) on the server and write their results.

    The server only runs code when its orgs.yaml allows it, since running the programs in your files is a different promise from reading them:

    server:
  babel:
    enable: true
    languages: ["python", "sh"]   # empty: every language orgs can run
    timeout: 30

    Without it the command explains that the server will not run source blocks. The local Org Exec Source Block commands still run code in Sublime.

    The connection

    Command What it does
    Org: Connect to orgs server find the server and log in
    Org: Log in to orgs log in again
    Org: Log out of orgs (forget stored login) log out and forget the stored login
    Org: Set orgs server url set orgsUrl and connect
    Org: orgs connection status the server, user, session and live updates
    Org: orgs reload server config have the server re-read its orgs.yaml

    Connecting and logging in are covered in Getting Started.

    Keeping files in sync

    The server reads your files from disk and Sublime edits buffers, so there are two copies of a file while you type. OrgEverywhere keeps them honest:

    • The server sees saved files. The agenda, search, backlinks and everything else that looks across files answer from what is saved. A modified buffer is not in them until you save it (the agenda counts the waiting buffers; agendaSaveBeforeRender saves them for you).
    • Edits by the server reload clean buffers. Refile, archive, agenda actions, clock out, capture and the rest have the server write the file; an open buffer without unsaved changes reloads with the new text. With orgsEvents (true) the server's change events keep notifications, the clock, ids and backlinks current when files change outside Sublime.
    • Dirty buffers are saved first. Before the server writes a file that is open with unsaved changes, OrgEverywhere saves it and waits for the server to read it, so the server's change is not lost by the next save of the buffer, nor your edits by the server's. With orgsSaveBeforeServerEdits set to false such a command refuses ("save the file first") instead, and you save yourself.

    A server on another machine sees its own paths: map them to yours with orgsPathMap.

    The Query Language

    Queries

    The orgs server answers questions about your headings in a small expression language: function calls joined with && (and), || (or) and ! (not), with brackets, numbers and comparisons (HabitStreak() > 7). A query is true or false for each heading; the headings it is true for are the answer.

    IsTodo() && HasTags("work")
IsTask() && !InTagGroup("HOME")
IsProject() && !IsArchived() && IsBlockedProject()
IsHabit() && HabitStreak() > 7
MatchHeadline("(?i)budget") || MatchContent("(?i)invoice")
IsDone() && OlderThan(30) && !IsArchived()

    Strings go in double or single quotes. Patterns are Go regular expressions ((?i) for case insensitive).

    OrgEverywhere uses queries in:

    • Org: orgs Query Search (a quick panel of the matches),
    • Org: Agenda Query (orgs) and OrgsQuery agenda views (see The Agenda),
    • saved queries (Org: orgs Save Query), shared with worg and the command line,
    • flashcard decks (Org: orgs Drill Flashcards).

    Filters

    {{Name}} in a query is replaced by the server's filter of that name, so filters build on each other. They are set in orgs.yaml:

    filters:
  AllTasks: "!IsProject() && IsTodo() && !IsArchived()"
  HomeTasks: "{{ AllTasks }} && InTagGroup('HOME')"

    The server comes with AllTasks, HomeTasks, WorkTasks, WorkProjects, Projects, ActiveProjects, StuckProjects, LooseTasks, NextTasks, DoneTasks, Clocked, Phone, Meetings and Notes; a filter of the same name in your orgs.yaml replaces one.

    Common functions

    State
    Function True for a heading that…
    IsTodo() has an active keyword (by its file's #+TODO)
    IsDone() has a done keyword
    HasAStatus() has any keyword
    IsStatus("WAITING") has that keyword
    IsTask() is an open todo, not a project and not archived
    IsNextTask() has a next keyword (NEXT, or the file's #+NEXT:)
    IsPriority("A") has that priority
    IsArchived() is tagged ARCHIVE, or is under such a heading
    Projects
    Function True for a heading that…
    IsProject() is a project
    IsBlockedProject() is a project without a next action
    IsPartOfProject() is inside a project
    Tags, properties and text
    Function True for a heading that…
    HasTags("a", "b") has all these tags (inherited ones count)
    HasTagMatching("^M[0-9]+$") has a tag matching the pattern
    InTagGroup("WORK") has a tag of that tag group (tagGroups in orgs.yaml)
    NoTags() has no tags
    HasProperty("EFFORT") has that property
    MatchProperty("OWNER", "^ian") has that property matching the pattern
    MatchHeadline("re") has a headline matching the pattern
    MatchContent("re") has a headline or text (not its children's) matching
    InFile("work") is in a file whose path matches the pattern
    Dates and clocks
    Function True for a heading that…
    HasScheduled(), HasDeadline(), HasTimestamp(), HasAnyDate() has that kind of date
    ScheduledPast(), DeadlinePast() has that date before today (a deadline today is not past)
    DeadlineWithin(3), ScheduledWithin(3) has that date between today and 3 days on
    Today(), Yesterday(), ThisWeek() is on the agenda that day, or in the seven days to today
    HasClock() has clock lines
    OlderThan(30) has its own date at least 30 days ago (DaysOld() is the number)
    Lists, links, habits and records
    Function True for a heading that…
    HasChecklist(), ChecklistDone() has checkboxes, all of them ticked (ChecklistLeft() counts the rest)
    HasTable(), HasBlock(), HasDrawer() holds a table, a block, a drawer
    HasLinks(), LinksTo("notes.org") links somewhere, to something matching
    HasBacklinks(), BacklinkCount() = 0= is linked to, or is an orphan
    HasBrokenLinks() holds a link that resolves to nothing
    IsHabit(), HabitStreak() > 7, MissedHabit() is a habit, on a streak, overdue
    IsRecord("contact"), InCollection("contact") is a record, is in a collection

    The full list is in the orgs server's documentation.

    Reference

    Every command and every setting, written beside the code that implements it.

    Commands

    Agenda

    Internal agenda commands

    org_agenda_re_render_view (args refilter, pos) redraws an agenda view from what was last fetched; the filter input and the agenda actions use it. org_tag_filtered_todo_view_internal (arg tags) is what Org Filtered Todo View runs. Neither is meant to be bound.

    Org Agenda Change Priority

    Command: org_agenda_change_priority Keys: , (in an agenda view)

    Sets the priority of the agenda entry under the cursor from a quick panel of priorities (default A to E) plus "none". Done by the orgs server in the heading's file, then the agenda is refetched. Needs the orgs server.

    Org Agenda Change Todo

    Command: org_agenda_change_todo Keys: s (in an agenda view); NeoVintageous normal mode: t

    Changes the todo state of the agenda entry under the cursor: a quick panel lists the states that heading's file allows (active and done, plus "none"), with the current one selected. The change is made by the orgs server in the heading's file (an open, modified buffer of that file is saved first) and the agenda is refetched. When the file changed since the agenda was drawn the heading is found again by its headline, and the command refuses when that is ambiguous. Needs the orgs server.

    Org Agenda Choose View

    Command: org_agenda_choose_custom_view Keys: none

    Lists the agendas defined in AgendaCustomViews in a quick panel and shows the one you pick (as Org Agenda Custom View).

    Org Agenda ClockIn

    Command: org_agenda_clock_in Keys: c i (in an agenda view)

    Clocks in to the agenda entry under the cursor. The server clocks out a running clock first and writes both CLOCK lines; open, modified buffers of those files are saved first. The clock is the server's, shared with every other orgs client. Needs the orgs server.

    Org Agenda ClockOut

    Command: org_agenda_clock_out Keys: c o (in an agenda view)

    Clocks out the running clock, wherever it is (not only the entry under the cursor), and refreshes the agenda; says so when no clock is running. Needs the orgs server.

    Org Agenda Custom View

    Command: org_agenda_custom_view Keys: alt+o o a (example global keymap); NeoVintageous normal mode: space o a Args: toShow (default "Default")

    Builds the agenda named toShow in AgendaCustomViews (the "Default" one is titled "Agenda"): each listed view, one under the other. Bind it with {"toShow": "Todos"} for a key per agenda. An unknown name raises an error in the console. Needs the orgs server.

    Org Agenda Day View

    Command: org_agenda_day_view Keys: alt+o a d (example global keymap); g in an agenda view; NeoVintageous normal mode: shift+space

    The default agenda: one "Agenda" view made of a three month calendar (days with entries highlighted), the week (an hour grid per day), today (scheduled and timed entries on an hour grid, deadlines, habits), blocked projects, projects with their NEXT tasks, and loose tasks (todos not in any project). Fetched from the orgs server; g rebuilds it (from any agenda view, g shows this day view). Unsaved org buffers are not in it; the view says how many (see agendaSaveBeforeRender).

    Settings: firstDayOfWeek, agendaWeekViewNumDays, agendaDayStartTime, agendaDayEndTime, agendaHeaderFormat, agendaProjectIs.

    Org Agenda Goto

    Command: org_agenda_go_to Keys: enter (in an agenda view)

    Opens the file of the agenda entry under the cursor at its heading.

    Org Agenda Goto Next Day / Prev Day

    Command: org_agenda_goto_next_day, org_agenda_goto_prev_day Keys: > / < (in an agenda view)

    Moves the agenda a day forward or back: the views are refetched for the new date and redrawn. Pressed quickly several times, only the newest fetch is drawn.

    Org Agenda Goto Split

    Command: org_agenda_go_to_split Keys: space (in an agenda view)

    Opens the agenda entry under the cursor in the other group, making a two column layout when the window has one group, so the agenda stays visible.

    Org Agenda Insert Assign

    Command: org_agenda_assign Keys: a (in an agenda view)

    Asks for the ASSIGNED property of the agenda entry under the cursor (prefilled with the current one) and sets it through the orgs server.

    Org Agenda Insert Effort

    Command: org_agenda_insert_effort Keys: e (in an agenda view)

    Asks for the EFFORT property of the agenda entry under the cursor (prefilled with the current one) and sets it through the orgs server. An empty answer changes nothing.

    Org Agenda Insert Id

    Command: org_agenda_id Keys: i (in an agenda view)

    Gives the agenda entry under the cursor an ID property (a new uuid) through the orgs server. A heading that already has one keeps it; the status bar shows it.

    Org Agenda Insert Tag

    Command: org_agenda_insert_tag Keys: t (in an agenda view, without NeoVintageous)

    Toggles a tag on the agenda entry under the cursor. A quick panel lists every tag the server and the local database know, marked [x] when the heading has it; "New tag…" asks for one. Picking a tag adds it or removes it. Needs the orgs server.

    Org Agenda Reopen Filter

    Command: org_agenda_re_open_filter_view Keys: alt+o f f (in an agenda view); NeoVintageous normal mode: f f (no palette entry)

    Opens the filter input of the todo lists in the current agenda view. As you type, only headings whose text matches the regular expression from their start are shown. Views that are not todo lists (calendar, week, day) have no filter.

    Org Filtered Todo View

    Command: org_tag_filtered_todo_view Keys: none

    Asks for a tag filter and shows the todo view ("Org Todos Filtered By: …") of the todos that pass it. The filter is space separated tags: TAG or +TAG must be present, |TAG at least one of these, -TAG must not be present. Needs the orgs server.

    Org Todo View

    Command: org_todo_view Keys: none

    Opens the "Org Todos" view: every heading in an active todo state that is not a project and not archived, from every file the orgs server knows, one per line (file, status, date, effort, heading…). Sorted by agendaTodoSortAscending. Type to filter when agendaTodoFilterByDefault is on, or open the filter with Org Agenda Reopen Filter. Run again from the view it refreshes in place, keeping the cursor. Needs the orgs server (without it the view says it is not connected).

    Org: Agenda Query (orgs)

    Command: org_agenda_query Keys: none Args: query, title

    Shows the headings matching an orgs query language expression in an agenda style view of their own ("Query: …"): file, status, date and heading per line; enter opens one, and the agenda actions (change todo, priority, tags, clock in…) work on its lines.

    Without query a quick panel offers "New query…" (prefilled with agendaOrgsQueryDefault), the queries run this session, your saved queries and the server's filters; whichever you pick can be edited before it runs. With query it runs at once, titled title. The palette entry "Org: Agenda All Tasks (orgs filter AllTasks)" runs {{AllTasks}}, the server filter of that name. A bad query shows the server's error in the view. Needs the orgs server.

    Capture

    Internal capture commands

    org_capture_base and org_server_move_base are base classes that Sublime also registers as commands; they do nothing useful on their own. Bind org_capture, org_refile, org_copy and friends instead.

    Org Archive All Done

    Command: org_archive_all_done Keys: none Args: onDone

    Archives every heading of the current file that is in a done state and not archived yet, in one request to the orgs server (each to its own archive location, as Org Archive Subtree). The file must be saved somewhere first. Says so when there is nothing to archive. Needs the orgs server.

    Org Archive Subtree

    Command: org_archive_subtree Keys: none Args: onDone

    Moves the heading at the cursor to its archive location, worked out by the orgs server: the heading's ARCHIVE property, else the file's #+ARCHIVE:, else the server's default (org's %s_archive::, i.e. file.org_archive). The source and archive buffers are saved first when open and modified. Needs the orgs server.

    Org Capture

    Command: org_capture Keys: ctrl+shift+x, alt+o z (example global keymap); NeoVintageous normal mode: Z

    Captures a note, todo or other text without leaving what you are doing. A quick panel lists the captureTemplates from your settings, then, when connected and orgsCaptureTemplates is on, the orgs server's templates (marked "orgs: ").

    A settings template fills the capture panel at the bottom of the window from its snippet (a .sublime-snippet in orgsnippets, built in or in Packages/User/orgsnippets; $0 is where the cursor ends up; the snippet gets ORG_INACTIVE_DATE, ORG_ACTIVE_DATE, ORG_DATE, ORG_TIME, ORG_CLIPBOARD, ORG_SELECTION, ORG_LINENUM and ORG_FILENAME) or its template text. Its target says where it goes: ["file", F] (end of file), ["file+headline", F, H] (under heading H, created if missing), ["file+olp", F, H1, H2...] (under an outline path), ["file+regexp", F, RE], ["file+olp+datetree", F, H1...] (under year / month / day headings, formats from the template's year-format, month-format, day-format properties), ["id", ID] (a heading's CUSTOM_ID, looked up on the orgs server) or ["clock"] (under the heading being clocked). F may use {refile} and {daypage} (today's day page). type is entry, item, checkitem, table-line or plain. With "openas": "direct" the target file itself is opened at the spot; otherwise ("panel") the panel's text is written into the target each time the panel loses focus, replacing what that capture wrote before.

    An orgs template is a form: each {{name}}, {{name|prompt}}, {{name|=default}} placeholder becomes a tab stop in the panel. The text is sent to the server once, when the panel loses focus with something typed; the server writes it to the template's target (that file is saved first if it is open and modified). If the server does not answer in time you are asked before it is sent again. Org: Abort Capture throws it away.

    Settings: captureTemplates, refile, captureBufferName, captureWriteFormat, orgsCaptureTemplates.

    Org Copy

    Command: org_copy Keys: none Args: onDone

    Copies the heading at the cursor (with its subtree) under another heading or to the end of a file. A quick panel lists the server's refile targets: every org file ("end of file") and its headings to orgsRefileDepth levels, shown as outline paths with todo state and tags. The orgs server writes the destination; open, modified buffers of both files are saved first. Copying a heading onto itself is refused. Needs the orgs server.

    Org Open Refile

    Command: org_open_refile Keys: ctrl+alt+x (example global keymap)

    Opens the file named by the refile setting, where captures land by default. Logs an error to the console when refile is not set.

    Org Refile

    Command: org_refile Keys: alt+o R; NeoVintageous normal mode: R Args: onDone

    Moves the heading at the cursor (with its subtree) under a heading picked from all refile targets (as Org Copy, to orgsRefileDepth levels) or to the end of a file. The orgs server rewrites both files and the buffers reload. Needs the orgs server.

    Org Refile File and Heading

    Command: org_refile_to_file_and_headline Keys: NeoVintageous normal mode: space r r Args: onDone

    Refiles in two steps: first pick the file, then the heading in it (all its headings, indented by level) or its end. Quicker than Org Refile with many files. Needs the orgs server.

    Org Refile To EOF

    Command: org_refile_to_file Keys: NeoVintageous normal mode: space r f Args: onDone

    Moves the heading at the cursor to the end of an org file picked from the files the orgs server knows. Needs the orgs server.

    Org: Abort Capture (orgs template)

    Command: org_capture_abort Keys: none

    Throws away the capture in progress in the capture panel instead of sending it, and hides the panel. Nothing in the panel is written anywhere afterwards. Meant for captures with an orgs server template, which are sent when the panel loses focus.

    Clocking

    Org Clear Clock

    Command: org_clear_clock Keys: none

    Offline only: forgets the running local clock without writing an end time (the open CLOCK line stays in the file). With the orgs server it refuses: the server clock is stopped with Org Clock Out.

    Org Clock In

    Command: org_clock_in Keys: alt+o c i; NeoVintageous normal mode: space c i Args: onDone

    Starts the clock on the heading at the cursor, clocking out a running clock first. With the orgs server the clock lives on the server, shared with every other orgs client (worg, the cli, other editors); the server writes the CLOCK line on clock out (open, modified buffers of the files involved are saved first). A clock left running from offline is closed first.

    Without a server the clock is local: an open CLOCK: [start]-- line is added to the heading's LOGBOOK drawer (or its property drawer with clockInPropertyBlock) and the clock is remembered in Packages/User/OrgEverywhere_Clocks.yaml.

    The running clock and its elapsed time show in the status bar of org views (clockShowInStatus).

    Org Clock Out

    Command: org_clock_out Keys: alt+o c o; NeoVintageous normal mode: space c o Args: onDone

    Stops the running clock, wherever it is. With the orgs server the server closes the clock and writes CLOCK: [start]--[end] => h:mm in the heading's drawer; a clock started while offline is closed locally first. Says so when no clock is running.

    Offline the open CLOCK line is closed in its file (opened if needed) and the file saved; with clockingSubMinuteClocks false a clock shorter than a minute is removed instead.

    Org Jump To Clock

    Command: org_jump_to_clock Keys: none Args: onDone

    Opens the heading the running clock is on (asking the server for it when connected). Says "No active clock" when none runs.

    Org Recalculate Clock

    Command: org_recalculate_clock Keys: none

    Rewrites every CLOCK line of the heading at the cursor, recomputing the h:mm duration of each from its start and end (after you edit a time by hand). Works on the buffer; no server needed. Uses the drawer chosen by clockInPropertyBlock. The cursor must be in a heading's section.

    Org Update Active Clock

    Command: org_update_clock Keys: none

    Offline only: after you edit the start time of the open CLOCK line by hand, reads it back as the running clock's start. With the orgs server it refuses (the server keeps the start; there is no open line).

    Connection

    Org: Connect to orgs server

    Command: orgs_connect Keys: none

    Finds the orgs server and logs in. The url is orgsUrl when it is set; otherwise each url in orgsDiscoverUrls is probed in order and the first orgs server that answers wins. A stored login (session token, or a remembered password hash) is reused; otherwise you are asked for a user name and password. When no server is found a dialog lists every url tried and why it failed.

    On success the file database is rebuilt from the server (the list of org files, ids, tags, backlinks). OrgEverywhere also connects by itself at startup, so this is for after the server was started late or moved.

    Settings: orgsEnabled, orgsUrl, orgsDiscoverUrls, orgsNoVerify, orgsCaFile, orgsTimeout.

    Org: Log in to orgs

    Command: orgs_login Keys: none

    Asks for a user name (offering the last one used, or orgsUser) and a password (typed masked), and logs in to the connected server. When no server has been found yet it connects first (as Org: Connect to orgs server). After a login the file database is rebuilt.

    Commands that need the server and find no login show "log in first" and open this prompt themselves; run the command again once logged in.

    Settings: orgsUser, orgsRememberLogin, orgsCredentialStore.

    Org: Log out of orgs (forget stored login)

    Command: orgs_logout Keys: none Args: forget (default true)

    Logs out of the server and stops listening for its change events. With forget (the default) the stored session token and the remembered password hash are deleted from the credential store too, so the next connect asks for a password. Bind it with {"forget": false} to keep them. Enabled only when a server has been found.

    Org: orgs

    Command: orgs_menu Keys: none

    Everything about the orgs connection in one quick panel: log in or out, check again, the connection status, open worg, change the server url, connect to the local server Org Everywhere for VS Code runs (when there is one), and the local orgs server (or set one up).

    Org: orgs connection status

    Command: orgs_status Keys: none

    Shows a dialog with the connection state (connected, login, searching, unavailable, disabled) and why; when a server is known also its url, the logged in user (or that the server runs without auth), when the session expires, which credential store holds the login, whether a password hash is remembered, whether live updates (the server's event stream) are connected, and how many files the server reports. With no server it lists the urls being tried.

    The same state, in short, is in the status bar of org views (orgsShowStatus).

    Org: orgs reload server config

    Command: orgs_reload_config Keys: none

    Asks the server to re-read its orgs.yaml (capture templates, filters, plugins…). The status bar shows the server's answer, including any settings that only take effect after the server is restarted. Needs the orgs server.

    Org: Set orgs server url

    Command: orgs_set_url Keys: none

    Asks for the server url (prefilled with orgsUrl, or http://localhost:8010), writes it to orgsUrl in your user OrgEverywhere settings, and connects to it. A trailing slash is dropped. An empty answer changes nothing.

    Day Pages

    Org Day Page Create

    Command: org_day_page_create Keys: alt+o d c (example global keymap); NeoVintageous normal mode: space d c Args: onDone

    Opens today's day page, creating it if it does not exist yet.

    With the orgs server the server owns day pages: its dayPagePath, dayPageMode and template decide the file, and when it makes today's page it carries the open tasks over from the last page and archives that one. OrgEverywhere then (with dayPageCopyTasksForToday) appends today's open tasks from other files: the open todos on today's agenda (scheduled, deadlines due or warning, dated), each heading with its text, skipping any already on the page. When the server has no dayPagePath the local settings below are used instead.

    Without a server (and with dayPagePath set) the page is made locally: dayPagePath/<dayPageNameFormat>.org, filled from the dayPageSnippet snippet; the previous page (looked for up to 90 days back) is tagged #+FILETAGS: ARCHIVE (dayPageArchiveOld) and its top level open todos copied over (dayPageCopyOpenTasks). Copying today's tasks from other files needs the server.

    Org Day Page Next

    Command: org_day_page_next Keys: alt+o d n; NeoVintageous normal mode: space d n Args: onDone

    Opens the next existing day page after the one shown. Stepping onto today opens (or creates) today's page, as Org Day Page Create; it never creates a page in the future. Says so when there is no later page.

    Org Day Page Previous

    Command: org_day_page_previous Keys: alt+o d p; NeoVintageous normal mode: space d p Args: onDone

    Opens the day page before the one shown (or before today, from any other file). With the orgs server it steps back by the server's day page increment (a day or a week) until a page exists, up to 60 steps. Locally it looks up to 90 days back; with dayPageCreateOldPages it opens (creating if needed) the page of the previous day instead.

    Dynamic Blocks

    Org Exec Dynamic Block

    Command: org_execute_dynamic_block Keys: alt+o c c (through Org Recalc, on the #+BEGIN: or #+END: line); vi command mode space c c

    With the cursor on the #+BEGIN: NAME :param value... line of a dynamic block, runs the block's writer and replaces everything between #+BEGIN: and #+END: with its output, indented to the heading. Writers: clocktable, columnview, insertdatetime (see Reference > Dynamic Blocks), plus any NAME.py in Packages/User/orgdynamic/. Run it on the #+BEGIN: line: on the #+END: line (which Org Recalc also accepts) the region comes out empty and the #+END: line itself is overwritten. This updates the block locally; Org: orgs Update Dynamic Blocks has the orgs server do it instead.

    Org: orgs Update Dynamic Blocks

    Command: org_orgs_update_dblocks Keys: none Args: all (default true)

    Has the server refresh the dynamic blocks (clocktable, columnview, …) of the current file: all of them, or with all false (palette: "Org: orgs Update Dynamic Block at Cursor") only the one at the cursor. The server rewrites the file and the buffer reloads. The buffer is saved first and must then match the file on disk exactly. Needs the orgs server.

    Editing

    Append text to the heading

    Command: org_append_text Keys: none (no palette entry) Args: text, onDone

    Appends text as a new line, indented two spaces per level, at the end of the current heading's subtree. Used by Org Link To Today; useful in key bindings.

    Append to a numbered list (internal)

    Commands: org_append_to_end_of_numbered_list, org_append_child_to_numbered_list Keys: none

    Variants of Org Append Numbered List that add the item further down the list (ctrl+shift+enter on a numbered item uses the same logic). Not in the command palette.

    Date picker keys

    Commands: org_date_picker_next_day / _prev_day, _next_week / _prev_week, _next_month / _prev_month, _next_hour / _prev_hour, _next_minute / _prev_minute

    Move the picked date while the date picker's input has focus:

    • > / < a day (palette: Org Date Next Day / Org Date Prev Day);
    • ctrl+. / ctrl+, a week;
    • alt+. / alt+, a month;
    • ctrl+shift+. / ctrl+shift+, an hour;
    • alt+shift+. / alt+shift+, a minute.
    Enter on a heading

    Command: org_enter_on_heading Keys: enter on a heading line Args: Indent (the heading level)

    enter on a heading starts the next line indented under the heading (level + 1 spaces) instead of at column 0. The keymap binds it per heading level 1 to 9 with the matching Indent.

    Insert checkbox / list item (internal)

    Commands: org_insert_checkbox, org_insert_unordered_list Keys: none (ctrl+enter and ctrl+shift+enter call them) Args: insertHere (default true: after the current line; false: after the item's last child).

    Adds a new - [ ] checkbox item / - list item at the same indent as the current one and puts the cursor at its end.

    Insert text as a child heading

    Command: org_insert_text_as_child_heading Keys: none (no palette entry) Args: heading, onDone

    Adds a child heading titled heading at the end of the current heading's subtree. Used by Org Link To Today; useful in your own key bindings or macros. As with Org Insert Heading Child the cursor must be under a heading.

    Insert the next item at the end (ctrl+shift+enter)

    Command: org_generic_insert_aux Keys: ctrl+shift+enter

    Like ctrl+enter, but list items are added after the item's last child (at the end of its sub list) rather than straight after the line, and on a heading a child heading is inserted (Org Insert Heading Child).

    Insert the next item here (ctrl+enter)

    Command: org_generic_insert Keys: ctrl+enter

    Inserts the next thing of the kind under the cursor, right after the current line: a new checkbox item on a checkbox line, a new - / + item in a plain list, the next number in a numbered list (renumbering the rest), otherwise a sibling heading (Org Insert Heading Sibling). Nothing happens before the first heading.

    Internal edit commands

    Commands: org_internal_erase (start, end), org_internal_replace (start, end, text), org_internal_insert (location, text); each also takes onDone.

    Used by other commands to change the buffer from a callback (Sublime only allows edits inside a command); after the edit the file is re-read. Not meant to be bound.

    Org Add Checkbox Summary

    Command: org_insert_checkbox_summary Keys: alt+o c s; vi command mode space c s

    Adds a [/] cookie at the end of the line (when it has none) and recalculates every summary in the buffer, so it reads [done/total] of the checkboxes below. Change it to [%] by hand for a percentage.

    Org Append Numbered List

    Command: org_append_numbered_list Keys: none (ctrl+enter on a numbered item does the same)

    Inserts a new numbered item after the current one and renumbers the list.

    Org Change Indent / Org Change DeIndent

    Commands: org_change_indent, org_change_de_indent Keys: alt+o right / alt+o left; vi command mode space right / space left

    On a list item (checkbox, plain or numbered) indents / outdents the item. On a heading demotes / promotes it (one star more / less).

    Org Change Priority

    Command: org_priority_change Keys: alt+o p; NeoVintageous normal mode: space p Args: onDone

    Sets the priority cookie ([#A]) of the heading at the cursor from a quick panel of the file's #+PRIORITIES: (or the priorities setting, default A to E) plus "none", which removes it.

    Org Change Todo

    Command: org_todo_change Keys: none Args: onDone

    Picks a new todo state for the heading at the cursor from a quick panel of the file's states (#+TODO: or todoStates) plus "none". Moving to a done state:

    • with a repeating SCHEDULED, DEADLINE or timestamp, the heading does not stay done: a - State "DONE" from "TODO" [stamp] line goes in its LOGBOOK, LAST_REPEAT is set, and each repeating timestamp moves on by its repeater (+ one step, ++ until in the future, .+ from today);
    • otherwise, with #+STARTUP: lognotedone you are asked for a note, logged in the LOGBOOK;
    • with #+STARTUP: logdone (or the logDone setting) a CLOSED: stamp is added. Leaving a done state removes the CLOSED: line.

    Works on the buffer; no server needed.

    Org Checkbox Toggle

    Command: org_toggle_checkbox Keys: alt+o t (through the toggle command)

    Toggles the checkbox on each selected line between [ ] and [x]. Children follow the parent, parents become [x] when all children are checked or [-] when some are, and the [/] / [%] summaries above are updated.

    Settings: checkboxSummaryRecursive.

    Org Closed

    Command: org_insert_closed Keys: none

    Adds a CLOSED: [now] line under the heading at the cursor.

    Org Copy Href / Org Select Href

    Command: org_copy_link_href, org_select_link_href Keys: none

    With the cursor on a link: copies (to the clipboard and the NeoVintageous register), or selects, the link's target, without the brackets and description.

    Org Create Heading Id

    Command: org_create_heading_id Keys: none Args: onDone.

    Gives the heading at the cursor an ID property with a new uuid, when it has none. Links and remote table references can then find it.

    Org Date Picker

    Command: org_date_picker Keys: none

    Opens the date picker on its own (a calendar view and a "Date:" input); on its own the picked date is not inserted anywhere. Commands that ask for a date (schedule, deadline, timestamps) open the same picker and use its answer. What you type is read as:

    • . or +0 now;
    • a number: that day of this month, or of next month when it has passed;
    • a duration (3d, 2h, 1d 4h, 1:30) from now;
    • a weekday (mon, fri…): the next one;
    • a month and/or day (dec 24, march): that date this year;
    • anything else as an org date (2026-10-11 Sun 10:00).

    The calendar follows as you type and a click (alt+click, see Org Setup Mouse Map) on a day picks it. Enter accepts, Escape cancels.

    Settings: firstDayOfWeek.

    Org Fix Tags

    Command: org_fix_tags Keys: NeoVintageous normal mode: space f m Args: onDone

    Realigns the tags of every heading in the file at tagColumn.

    Org Insert Archive Tag

    Command: org_insert_archive_tag Keys: none Args: onDone

    Adds the ARCHIVE tag to the heading at the cursor (as Org Insert Tag). To move a heading to its archive file use Org Archive Subtree.

    Org Insert Created Property

    Command: org_insert_created_property Keys: none Args: onDone.

    Sets the heading's Created property to the current time as an inactive timestamp ([2026-10-11 Sun 14:03]).

    Org Insert CustomId

    Command: org_insert_custom_id Keys: alt+o i i; NeoVintageous normal mode: space i i Args: onDone

    Asks for a CUSTOM_ID (completing from the ids the orgs server knows) and sets it as a property of the heading at the cursor. Spaces become -.

    Org Insert Date Inactive / Org Insert Date Active

    Command: org_insert_date_inactive, org_insert_date_active Keys: alt+o i d i / alt+o i d a; NeoVintageous normal mode: space i d i / space i d a

    Opens the date picker and inserts the date and time you pick at the cursor, inactive ([...]) or active (<...>).

    Org Insert Drawer

    Command: org_insert_drawer Keys: none

    Asks for a name and adds an empty :NAME: … :END: drawer to the heading at the cursor, unless it already has one of that name.

    Org Insert Effort

    Command: org_insert_effort Keys: none Args: onDone.

    Asks for an effort estimate (offering the current EFFORT value) in org duration form (1d 3h, 2h, 45min, 1:30). A plain number gets the unit from defaultEffortEstimateUnit. Stores it, normalised, in the heading's Effort property. The agenda and timesheets read it.

    Settings: defaultEffortEstimateUnit.

    Org Insert Heading Child

    Command: org_insert_heading_child Keys: alt+o i c; NeoVintageous normal mode: space i c Args: onDone

    Inserts a heading one level deeper at the end of the current heading's subtree (its last child), from the headingN snippet. The cursor must be on or under a heading: above the first heading of a file that has headings the command fails (an error in the console).

    Org Insert Heading Sibling

    Command: org_insert_heading_sibling Keys: alt+o i h; NeoVintageous normal mode: space i h

    Inserts a new heading at the same level after the current heading and all its children, from the headingN snippet, so the cursor lands in its title. Above the first heading it adds a level 1 heading at the end of the file.

    Org Insert Property

    Command: org_insert_property Keys: none Args: name, value (skip the prompts), onDone.

    Asks for a property name and a value and sets it in the heading's :PROPERTIES: drawer (the drawer is created when missing, an existing value replaced).

    Org Insert Property Drawer

    Command: org_insert_property_drawer Keys: none

    Adds an empty :PROPERTIES: drawer to the heading at the cursor when it has none.

    Org Insert Tag

    Command: org_insert_tag Keys: NeoVintageous normal mode: space i m Args: text, onDone

    Adds a tag to the heading at the cursor and aligns the tags at tagColumn. Without text an input with completion offers every tag the orgs server knows (or, offline, the tags of the open files). A tag the heading already has is left alone. (alt+o i t is also bound to it in the keymap, but the later org_active_timestamp binding of the same keys wins.)

    Org Insert Today / Now (Active / Inactive)

    Command: org_insert_today_inactive, org_insert_today_active, org_insert_now_inactive, org_insert_now_active Keys: none

    Inserts today's date ([2024-05-01 Wed] inactive, <2024-05-01 Wed> active) or the date and time ([2024-05-01 Wed 14:30]) at the cursor.

    Org Jump To Marker

    Command: org_jump_to_marker Keys: none Args: name

    Opens the heading that carries a marker (picked as in Org Set Marker). For the today marker a heading with :CUSTOM_ID: TODAY is used when no heading carries it (the way "today" was found before markers); offline only open buffers are searched for that.

    Org Jump To Today

    Command: org_jump_to_today Keys: none

    Opens the heading carrying the today marker (orgsTodayMarker): Org Jump To Marker for that marker, falling back to a :CUSTOM_ID: TODAY heading.

    Org Link To Today

    Command: org_link_to_today Keys: none Args: onDone

    Files the heading at the cursor under today's heading: it is scheduled for now (SCHEDULED: added), a child heading with the same title is added under the heading carrying the today marker, and a link back to the heading (as Org Create Link) is appended under it. The today file is opened in the background, edited and saved. Needs the orgs server to find the today marker (or an open buffer with :CUSTOM_ID: TODAY).

    Org Move Heading Up / Org Move Heading Down

    Command: org_move_heading_up, org_move_heading_down Keys: alt+o up / alt+o down; NeoVintageous normal mode: space up / space down

    Swaps the heading at the cursor (with its subtree) with its previous or next sibling. Does nothing when there is no sibling that way.

    Org Recalc

    Command: org_recalc Keys: alt+o c c; vi command mode space c c

    The "do what I mean" update. On a dynamic block's #+BEGIN: or #+END: line: Org Exec Dynamic Block. On inline source code: Org Exec Inline Source Block. In a source block: Org Exec Source Block. On a #+CALL: line: Org Execute Call. In a table: runs the table's formulas. Anywhere else: recalculates every checkbox summary in the buffer and renumbers the numbered list at the cursor.

    Org Recalc Checkbox / Org Recalc All Checkbox

    Commands: org_recalc_checkbox_summary, org_recalc_all_checkbox_summaries Keys: none

    Recount the [/] / [%] cookie under the cursor (on each selection that is on a cookie) or every cookie in the buffer. Org Recalc does the whole buffer too.

    Org Remove All Tags

    Command: org_remove_all_tags Keys: NeoVintageous normal mode: space r a m Args: onDone

    Removes every tag from the heading at the cursor.

    Org Remove Tag

    Command: org_remove_tag Keys: NeoVintageous normal mode: space r m Args: text, onDone

    Removes a tag (asked for with completion, or text) from the heading at the cursor, case insensitively, and realigns the rest.

    Org Schedule / Org Deadline / Org Timestamp

    Command: org_schedule, org_deadline, org_active_timestamp Keys: alt+o i s / alt+o i e / alt+o i t; NeoVintageous normal mode: space i s / space i e / space i t Args: dateval

    Adds a line under the heading at the cursor with SCHEDULED: <date>, DEADLINE: <date> or a plain active timestamp, the date picked with the date picker (cancelling removes the line). dateval (a date string) skips the picker. An existing SCHEDULED or DEADLINE line is not replaced: a second one is added. (org_base_timestamp is their shared base and not a command to bind.)

    Org Select Entity / Org Copy Entity

    Command: org_select_entity, org_copy_entity Keys: alt+o m e / alt+o y e; NeoVintageous normal mode: space m e / space y e

    Selects, or copies, the heading at the cursor and its own text, without its children.

    Org Select Subtree / Org Copy Subtree

    Command: org_select_subtree, org_copy_subtree Keys: alt+o m s / alt+o y s; NeoVintageous normal mode: space m s / space y s

    Selects, or copies to the clipboard (and the NeoVintageous register), the heading at the cursor with all its children. Does nothing above the first heading.

    Org Set Marker

    Command: org_set_marker Keys: none Args: name, onDone

    Puts a marker on the heading at the cursor: one of orgsMarkers (plus the today marker), picked from a quick panel when there is more than one, or name. The previous holder loses the tag (its file is saved first if it is open and modified). Needs the orgs server.

    Org Set Today

    Command: org_set_today Keys: none Args: onDone

    Puts the today marker (orgsTodayMarker, default TODAY) on the heading at the cursor. A marker is a tag the orgs server keeps on exactly one heading: the heading that had it loses it. Org Link To Today and the other "today" commands work on the heading carrying it. Needs the orgs server.

    Org Sort List

    Command: org_sort_list Keys: none

    Sorts the plain or numbered list at the cursor alphabetically by each item's first line, keeping each item's continuation lines with it. A numbered list is renumbered afterwards. Logs an error when the cursor is not in a list.

    Org Update Numbered List

    Command: org_update_numbered_list Keys: none (Org Recalc does it)

    Renumbers the numbered list (1. or 1)) at the cursor from 1, level by level, keeping each item's separator.

    Reformat the file with the orgs server

    Command: org_orgs_reformat_file Keys: none (no palette entry)

    Has the server rewrite the current file in its canonical layout (aligned tags, property drawers, planning lines); the buffer reloads with the result. The buffer is saved first and the file on disk must then be exactly the buffer, or it refuses. Needs the orgs server.

    Toggle checkbox or todo

    Command: org_toggle Keys: alt+o t; vi command mode space t (that binding is limited to tables by its context)

    On a checkbox line toggles the checkbox (Org Checkbox Toggle); anywhere else changes the heading's todo state (Org Change Todo).

    Exporting

    Org Download Highligh Js

    Command: org_download_highligh_js Keys: none

    Downloads highlight.js into Packages/User/highlightjs/. The html exporter now links highlight.js from a CDN, so this is only needed for an offline copy.

    Org Export File As Dnd

    Command: org_export_file_as_dnd_pdf Keys: none

    Despite the name it does not export: it downloads the DND 5e LaTeX template (github rpgtex/DND-5e-LaTeX-Template) and unzips it, a first step towards Dungeons and Dragons styled pdfs. Then use #+LATEX_CLASS: dndbook (or similar) with Org Export File As Pdf once the template is installed where your TeX finds it.

    Org Export File As Html

    Command: org_export_file_org_html Keys: none Args: index (export only that heading, as Org Export Subtree As Html passes), suffix (added to the output name), onDone.

    Exports the whole file to NAME.html next to it with OrgEverywhere's own html exporter (no pandoc needed). When htmlExecuteSourceOnExport is true (the default) every source block is run first, so results are current. See Reference > Exporting > Html export options.

    Settings: htmlExecuteSourceOnExport, htmlDefaultSkipSrc, HtmlStyle, imageSearchPath.

    Org Export File As Latex

    Command: org_export_file_as_latex Keys: none Args: index, suffix, onDone (as Org Export File As Pdf).

    Exports the file to NAME.tex next to it with OrgEverywhere's latex exporter (see Reference > Exporting > Latex export options). Source blocks are run first only when latexExecuteSourceOnExport is true.

    Org Export File As Pdf

    Command: org_export_file_as_pdf Keys: none Args: index (export one heading), suffix (added to the output name), onDone.

    Exports the file to NAME.tex (as Org Export File As Latex) and runs latex2Pdf on it in the file's folder, producing NAME.pdf. The .tex file is left in place. Errors from the latex run only reach the debug log, so run the .tex by hand when no pdf appears.

    Settings: latex2Pdf, latexClass, latexExecuteSourceOnExport.

    Org Export File As Reveal Js

    Command: org_export_file_reveal_js Keys: none Args: index (export one heading), suffix (added to the output name), onDone.

    Exports the file to NAME.html next to it as a reveal.js presentation (see Reference > Exporting > Reveal.js export options). reveal.js and its plugins (markdown, highlight, search, zoom, notes, math) are loaded from REVEAL_LOCATION, by default a CDN, so showing it needs network access. Source blocks are run first when revealExecuteSourceOnExport is true.

    Settings: revealExecuteSourceOnExport, revealDefaultSkipSrc, htmlDefaultSkipSrc, the Reveal... settings.

    Org Export Subtree As Html

    Command: org_export_subtree_as_org_html Keys: none Args: onDone (internal callback).

    Exports only the heading at the cursor and its children with the html exporter, to NAME_subtree.html next to the file. The file level keywords (title, style…) still apply.

    Org Pandoc File To Html

    Command: org_export_file_as_html Keys: none

    Exports the file to NAME.html next to it with pandoc (pandoc -s -c STYLE.css [-H STYLE_inheader.html] -o NAME.html NAME.org). The style comes from PandocStyle; its css and in-header file are taken from Packages/OrgEverywhere/pandoc/ (only blocky ships). The file is exported as saved on disk. Pandoc's errors are shown in a dialog.

    Settings: PandocPath, PandocStyle.

    Org Pandoc Subtree To Html

    Command: org_export_subtree_as_html Keys: none

    Meant to export the heading at the cursor with pandoc (copied to a temporary file, with a #+TITLE: added when it has none). Currently broken: the command line is lost before pandoc runs, so it fails with an error. Use Org Export Subtree As Html instead.

    Org: orgs Export File

    Command: org_orgs_export Keys: none Args: kind, theme, open

    Exports the current file with one of the orgs server's exporters (the ones in server.exporters of its orgs.yaml: html, latex, reveal.js, impress.js, mermaid, markdown…) and writes the result next to the file. A quick panel lists the exporters, plus pdf when the server has latex; kind skips it (the palette's "Org: orgs Export File as PDF" passes "pdf"). For html and slide exporters with more than one theme you pick a theme, or the file's own; theme skips that.

    The output is file.html, file.tex, file.md, file.pdf…; slide decks and other html exporters get file.KIND.html so they do not overwrite the plain html. The buffer is saved and synced to the server first. Afterwards, depending on open (default orgsExportOpen): "ask" offers to open it, "always" opens it (html, pdf and svg in the browser, anything else in Sublime), "never" only reports the path. Needs the orgs server and a buffer with a file.

    Read the org export (unfinished)

    Command: org_export_file_read_the_org Keys: none

    Not in the command palette. An early copy of the reveal.js exporter (reveal.js 3.8 from cdnjs) meant to become a "read the org" style html export. It does not run: it fails on an undefined name before writing anything.

    Folding

    Org Fold All

    Command: org_fold_all Keys: none

    Folds every heading of the file (the OVERVIEW state of Tab cycling).

    Org Fold All Links

    Command: org_fold_all_links Keys: none

    Folds the target part of every [[target][description]] link so only the description shows. Done automatically when a file opens and after each Tab fold; Tab on a link toggles that one link.

    Org Fold Contents

    Command: org_fold_contents Keys: none

    Meant to show every heading with its text folded (the CONTENTS state of Tab cycling). Currently broken: it fails on an undefined name after removing all folds. Shift+Tab on a heading cycles through CONTENTS.

    Org Fold Others

    Command: org_fold_all_but_me Keys: vi command mode space f o

    Unfolds the heading at the cursor and folds every sibling of it and of each of its ancestors, leaving only the path to the cursor open.

    Org Fold Thing

    Command: org_fold_thing Keys: none

    Folds the selected text (Sublime's own fold of the selection).

    Org Global Tab Cycling

    Command: org_global_tab_cycling Keys: shift+tab (on a heading)

    Cycles the whole file: OVERVIEW (top headings only) to CONTENTS (all headings, text folded) to SHOW ALL (drawers and links still folded) and back. In a table shift+tab moves to the previous field instead.

    Org Remove All Folds

    Command: org_remove_all_folds Keys: none

    Removes every fold in the buffer, links and drawers included. The way out when folds get confused (for example after the file changed on disk).

    Org Tab Cycling

    Command: org_tab_cycling Keys: tab (in an org file, on a heading, link, checkbox, block, table or the file's top)

    Tab does what fits the cursor's place:

    • on a heading: cycles FOLDED, CHILDREN (children shown folded), SUBTREE (all open);
    • on a drawer or a block line inside a heading: folds / unfolds it;
    • before the first heading: cycles the whole file like Shift+Tab;
    • on a link: folds / unfolds the link's target;
    • in a table: moves to the next field (Table Editor);
    • on a checkbox with children: folds / unfolds the children;
    • otherwise: inserts the best completion, or a tab.

    The file is re-read first when it changed.

    Org Unfold All

    Command: org_unfold_all Keys: none

    Unfolds every heading of the file. Drawers and links folded inside headings stay as they are; Org Remove All Folds opens everything.

    Links

    File name completion inside a link

    Keys: the completion popup (as you type, or ctrl+space)

    Inside [[...]] the completion list offers the org files whose path matches what is typed after the [[ (as a regular expression, or plain text when it is not a valid one). Picking one inserts file:RELATIVE/PATH][ with the cursor ready for the description. The file list comes from the orgs server (cached).

    Jump to an ID

    Command: org_jump_to_id Keys: none (no palette entry)

    As Org Jump To CustomId, for ID properties. Needs the orgs server.

    Org Create Link

    Command: org_create_link Keys: alt+o y l (example global keymap); NeoVintageous normal mode: space y l

    Puts a link to where the cursor is on the clipboard (and the NeoVintageous register), to paste somewhere else. In an org file it links, in this order: a <<target>> or #+NAME: on the line, the heading's ID, its CUSTOM_ID, the heading by title, else the row and column. In any other file it links the row and column.

    Org Hide Images

    Command: org_hide_images Keys: none Args: onDone

    Removes every inline image from the view.

    Org Jump To Backlink

    Command: org_jump_to_backlinks Keys: none

    Lists the links in other files that point at the current file (from the orgs server's link index): their description, and the file title, line and heading they are in. Picking one jumps there. Needs the orgs server.

    Org Jump To CustomId

    Command: org_jump_to_custom_id Keys: none

    Lists every CUSTOM_ID the orgs server knows (id, heading and file) and opens the one you pick; when the file is open the row comes from the buffer, which may have moved the heading since the server read it. Needs the orgs server.

    Org Link To File

    Command: org_link_to_file Keys: none

    Inserts a [[file:...][title]] link to another org file at the cursor, relative to this file. The quick panel lists every org file the orgs server knows, with its #+TITLE: and, with linkFindUseRoamTags, its #+ROAM_TAGS: in parentheses. The description is the title (with the roam tags when insertRoamTagToFileLink is on), or the file name. Needs the orgs server.

    Org Open Link

    Command: org_open_link Keys: enter on a link (when the completion popup is not showing)

    Follows the link under the cursor. A link whose protocol the local resolvers do not know (anything but file, id, http, https, mailto, email, cmd, prompt, and jira / j once resolver.jira.url is set) is offered to the orgs server first, which resolves it with its linkProtocols config: to a url (opened in the browser; anything but http(s) asks first) or a command (always asks before running it). When the server does not know it either, or is not connected, the local resolvers in linkResolvers are tried in order:

    • internal: [[id:...]], [[#custom-id]], [[*Heading]], a <<target>> or #+NAME: in this file. Ids are looked up on the orgs server.
    • http / https: opened with the system opener.
    • prompt: cmd:DIR / prompt:DIR opens a terminal there.
    • jira: jira:KEY / j:KEY opens resolver.jira.url with the key.
    • email: mailto:ADDR/SUBJECT opens your mail program (email: links are not implemented).
    • file: file:path, with ::row::col, ::#custom-id, ::*heading or ::text (target, name or heading); relative to the file, ~ and environment variables expanded. Files matching file_exclude_patterns open in the system's application instead of Sublime.

    An unresolvable link shows an error dialog.

    Org Search Links

    Command: org_search_links Keys: none

    Lists every link in every org file the orgs server knows (description and target, with file, line and heading) and jumps to the one you pick, previewing as you move. Needs the orgs server.

    Org Show Backlinks

    Command: org_show_backlinks Keys: none

    Opens a "Backlinks" view beside the file: the links pointing at it, grouped by source file (by title), each an org link to its line with the heading path, broken links marked. While it is showing it follows the org file you switch to, and refreshes when files are saved or the server re-reads them (backlinksUpdate). Needs the orgs server.

    Org Show Image / Org Hide Image

    Command: org_show_image, org_hide_image Keys: none

    Shows or hides the inline image of the link under the cursor only.

    Org Show Images

    Command: org_show_images Keys: none Args: onDone

    Shows every image link in the view inline, below its line, scaled to at most 1024 pixels wide. Local images are looked for relative to the file, then in imageSearchPath, then in an images folder of each org directory; http(s) images are downloaded once and cached (the cache list is Packages/User/OrgEverywhere_image_cache.yaml). A #+ORG_ATTR: with :width / :height above the link, or {width… height=…}= after it, sets the size. #+STARTUP: inlineimages (or startup) shows them when the file opens.

    Redisplay inline images

    Command: org_cycle_images Keys: none (no palette entry) Args: onDone

    Hides and then shows again every inline image in the view (Org Hide Images then Org Show Images), keeping the cursor; for after an image file changed on disk.

    Local orgs Server

    Org: Copy Local orgs Server Password

    Command: orgs_copy_server_password Keys: none

    Copies the password Sublime keeps for sublimetext, to log in by hand. Adding a user of your own (Org: Manage orgs Users) is the better way.

    Org: Edit Local orgs Server Config

    Command: orgs_edit_server_config Keys: none

    Opens the local server's orgs.yaml. Saving it has the server reload it at once; when something you changed needs a restart (the port, orgDirs, the keystore) Sublime says so and offers to restart it.

    Org: Local orgs Server

    Command: orgs_server_menu Keys: none

    The local server's menu, headed by its version, address and whether it is running: start or restart, stop, check for an update, edit its config, show its log, open worg in the browser (logged in for you), trust its certificate in browsers, use it from a terminal, users and passwords, copy its password, and connect to it when orgsUrl points elsewhere. Sets one up when there is none (Org: Set Up a Local orgs Server).

    Org: Manage orgs Users

    Command: orgs_manage_users Keys: none

    Gives you a login of your own, for worg in a browser or orgs login somewhere else. For the local server it lists its users (administrator, last login) and offers:

    • Add a user: name, password (typed masked, twice), ordinary user or administrator. Added over the wire (POST /users/add), so it works at once; the password does not travel, a salted hash of it does.
    • On a user: Change the password or Remove. These edit the keystore with the orgs user command line, so the server is stopped for the moment it takes.

    sublimetext is Sublime's own login and is left alone. For a server that is not the local one, adding a user is all there is, and needs your login to be an administrator there.

    Org: Set Up a Local orgs Server

    Command: orgs_set_up_server Keys: none

    Downloads the latest orgs release from github for this machine, checks it against the release's checksums.txt, and runs it in the background, reading a folder of org files you pick (one of the project's folders, or any other). It writes an orgs.yaml, a keystore and a self-signed certificate beside it, serves https only and answers this machine only. orgsUrl is pointed at it.

    It then asks how you want to log in:

    • Log me in automatically: the user sublimetext gets a random password, kept in your OS keychain, and Sublime logs in with it. You are never asked (orgsServerAutoLogin).
    • Ask me to log in: you pick a user name and password of your own (an administrator). Sublime asks for them like any other server's login.

    Once set up, the command opens the local server's menu instead (Org: Local orgs Server).

    Org: Show Local orgs Server Log

    Command: orgs_show_server_log Keys: none

    Opens what the local server printed since it was last started from Sublime.

    Org: Start / Stop / Restart Local orgs Server

    Commands: orgs_start_server, orgs_stop_server, orgs_restart_server Keys: none

    The server runs detached, so it outlives the Sublime that started it and every window shares it. Sublime starts it by itself when it opens (orgsServerAutoStart). Stop only stops a server this set up; anything else answering on its port is left alone.

    Org: Trust Local orgs Server Certificate in Browsers

    Command: orgs_trust_server_certificate Keys: none

    Browsers warn about the local server's self-signed certificate until it is trusted. On macOS this adds it to your login keychain, on Windows to your user's root store; each asks you first. On Linux each browser keeps its own list, so it tells you where to import it. Do it again after the certificate is renewed (every couple of years).

    Org: Update Local orgs Server

    Command: orgs_update_server Keys: none

    Looks for a newer orgs release on github. When there is one it is downloaded and checked like at set up, the server is stopped, the binary replaced and the server started again. Once a day Sublime also looks by itself and offers a new release (orgsServerCheckForUpdates): update, read the release notes, skip that version, or not now.

    Org: Use the Local orgs Server from a Terminal

    Command: orgs_server_terminal Keys: none

    The orgs command line beside the server reads its orgs.yaml, keys and all, so it makes its own token and needs no login. This shows where it is and copies an alias for your shell: alias orgs'<path>'=.

    Misc

    Input box choices

    Commands: org_input_down, org_input_up Keys: down / up (in an OrgEverywhere input box)

    Some prompts (tags, custom ids, file names in Org Import Csv…) show the matching choices in a popup under the input; down and up move through them and put the current one in the input. What you type filters the list (spaces match anything).

    Settings: input_font_face.

    Internal startup commands

    org_on_load_sync_up runs once after the plugin loads: it applies the startup folding (and inline images) to every org file already open in the window. It can be run again by hand after changing startup, but is not meant to be bound.

    Mouse handler

    Command: org_mouse_handler Keys: alt+click, once the mouse map is set up

    Turns a click into an "orgmouse" event for the plugin; today the date picker uses it (alt+click a day in its calendar). Sublime has no mouse binding for it by default: Org Setup Mouse Map writes one.

    NeoVintageous clipboard

    When NeoVintageous is installed, the copy commands (Org Copy Subtree, Org Copy Entity, Org Copy Href…) also put the text in NeoVintageous's 0 register, so p pastes it. Without NeoVintageous nothing extra happens.

    Org Beancount Create

    Command: beancount_new_file Keys: none

    Opens a new buffer with OrgEverywhere's org-beancount syntax.

    Org Beancount Transaction

    Command: beancount_new_transaction Keys: none

    Inserts the transaction snippet of the Beancount package (Packages/Beancount/snipets/transaction.sublime-snippet) filled with today's date, the clipboard, the selection and the file name; the default currency is CAD. Needs the Beancount package. Auto indent is switched off while the snippet goes in, and NeoVintageous is put in insert mode.

    Org Choose Timesheet Table

    Command: org_choose_timesheet Keys: none Args: onDone.

    A quick panel of the AgendaCustomViews names; then inserts that timesheet (as Org Timesheet Table). Every name currently gives the same todo based sheet.

    Org Create Color Scheme From Active

    Command: org_create_color_scheme_from_active Keys: none

    Copies your current color scheme (.sublime-color-scheme or .tmTheme) to Packages/User/OrgColorSchemes/NAME_Org.sublime-color-scheme with OrgEverywhere's scopes added (todo states, priorities, block fences, the agenda and the date picker), and makes it the color scheme of org files, the agenda and the date picker (color_scheme in OrgEverywhere, orgagenda and orgdatepicker settings).

    Org Internal Keymap Gen

    Command: org_create_keymap_doc Keys: none

    Developer tool: builds a table of the palette commands and their keys (normal and vi) from the package's OrgEverywhere.sublime-commands and Default.sublime-keymap.

    Org Internal Syntax Gen

    Command: org_regen_syntax_template Keys: none

    Developer tool: regenerates OrgEverywhere.sublime-syntax from OrgEverywhere.sublime-syntax-template inside an unpacked package folder. Not useful in an installed (zipped) package.

    Org New File

    Command: org_new_file Keys: none

    Opens a new, unsaved buffer with the org syntax set. Org: orgs New File from Template makes a file in one of the orgs server's directories instead.

    Org Rebuild Db

    Command: org_rebuild_db Keys: none

    Forgets what OrgEverywhere has cached: the parses of buffers and closed files, and the orgs server's answers (file list, ids, tags), which are asked for again. Nothing is scanned locally: the orgs server is the database of which org files exist. Connecting or logging in does this by itself.

    Org Reload File

    Command: org_reload_file Keys: none

    Re-parses the current buffer. Normally not needed: a buffer is re-parsed when it changes or is saved.

    Org Select Color Scheme

    Command: org_select_existing_color_scheme Keys: none

    A quick panel of the schemes in Packages/User/OrgColorSchemes/ plus the bundled OrgEverywhere and OrgEverywhere-Light schemes; the one picked becomes the color scheme of org files, the agenda and the date picker.

    Org Setup Mouse Map

    Command: org_setup_mouse_map Keys: none (not in the command palette)

    Writes Packages/User/Default.sublime-mousemap binding alt+click to org_mouse_handler (keeping the normal click to place the cursor), only when that file does not exist yet. Run it from the console: view.run_command("org_setup_mouse_map").

    Org Show TestFile / Org Show Table Tests / Org Show Source Tests

    Commands: org_show_testfile, org_show_table_tests, org_show_source_block_tests Keys: none

    Each opens a copy of a sample org file that ships with the package (tests/testfile.org, tests/tableunittests.org, tests/sourceunittests.org) and asks where to save it. The table and source files double as worked examples of formulas and source blocks.

    Org Show Worklog

    Command: org_build_dev_docs Keys: none

    Opens a new org buffer with every release note (messages/VERSION.org), newest first: the change log.

    Org Test Durations

    Command: org_test_duration Keys: none

    A developer check: parses sample durations (2y3d5h6min, 1d 3:44…) and prints them to the console. Durations elsewhere use the same syntax: numbers with y, d, h, min, and an optional H:MM or H:MM:SS part at the end.

    Org Test Template

    Command: org_test_template Keys: none

    A developer check: prints a few expanded templates (date, time, file name, a setting) to the console.

    Org Timesheet Google Gantt

    Command: org_generate_google_gantt_chart Keys: none Args: toShow (skip the view picker), onDone.

    Builds the timesheet and writes timesheetPath/project_schedule.html, a Google Charts gantt chart (open it in a browser; it loads the chart library from Google). Resources are the assignees (done for finished tasks), dependencies come from AFTER / ORDERED.

    Needs the orgs server. Settings: timesheetPath, timesheetDefaultStartDate.

    Org Timesheet Mermaid Gantt

    Command: org_generate_mermaid_gantt_chart Keys: none Args: toShow (skip the view picker), onDone.

    Builds the timesheet (as Org Timesheet Table) and writes it as a mermaid gantt chart to timesheetPath/schedule.mermaid (excluding weekends, grouped into sections by the SECTION property, a file #+SECTION: or timesheetDefaultSection), then renders timesheetPath/project_schedule.png with mermaidPath. An ASSIGNED of A, C, M, X or Y marks the task active, critical, milestone, critical done or critical active. Tasks with no date start at timesheetDefaultStartDate. Rendering runs on Windows and macOS only.

    Needs the orgs server. Settings: timesheetPath, mermaidPath, timesheetDefaultSection, timesheetDefaultStartDate.

    Org Timesheet Table

    Command: org_insert_timesheet Keys: none Args: toShow (an AgendaCustomViews name, default Default), onDone.

    Asks the orgs server for every todo and done heading (not archived, not projects) and inserts a table at the cursor with one row per task: Name, Estimate (the EFFORT property), Start (scheduled, else deadline, else first timestamp), End (start plus the estimate), Dep (the row it waits for), Assigned, Spent (clocked time of the heading and its sub headings) and X (done). A task waits for the heading named by its AFTER property (an ID), or, under a parent with an ORDERED property, for the sibling before it.

    Assigned comes from the heading's ASSIGNED property, else a file #+ASSIGNED:, else timesheetDefaultAssigned. Needs the orgs server. The org_render_timesheet command draws the table once the answer arrives (internal).

    Settings: timesheetDefaultAssigned, AgendaCustomViews.

    Org Trello Sync Board

    Command: org_trello_sync_board Keys: none

    Needs the Trello package (it only exists when that package imports). Meant to rebuild the board named by the file's #+TRELLO: BOARD-ID line, or, without one, to offer your boards and write the chosen one to a new trello_NAME.org buffer: a TODO/DONE heading per list, a heading per card (labels as tags, due date as SCHEDULED, TRELLOID / URL / MEMBERS properties, description), checklists as checkbox lists and comments as sub headings. Currently broken from an org file: reading the #+TRELLO: tag fails (the module never imports its settings), so run it from a non org buffer to author a new board page.

    Settings: trello (a default board id list).

    Swiper date picker (experimental)

    Commands: a_org_date_picker, a_org_date_picker_next_day, _prev_day, _next_week, _prev_week, _next_month, _prev_month Keys: none

    An unfinished copy of the date picker, kept for experiments. Not in the command palette or the keymap; use Org Date Picker.

    Navigation

    Org Jump In File

    Command: org_jump_in_file Keys: none

    A quick panel of every heading in the file; picking one moves the cursor to it (keeping the cursor's column) and centres it.

    Org Up / Org Down

    Commands: org_up, org_down Keys: ctrl+up, ctrl+down (in an org file)

    Moves the cursor to the previous / next heading line (any level) and centres it.

    Notifications

    Org Agenda Rebuild Notices

    Command: org_rebuild_notifications Keys: none

    Rebuilds today's reminder list from the orgs server's agenda now (starting the notification thread if it is not running), instead of waiting for the next periodic rebuild. Needs the orgs server.

    Show the notifications view

    Command: org_show_notifications Keys: none (no palette entry)

    Draws the "Notifications" view: the reminders raised so far today. The notification thread runs it itself each time it raises a reminder; running it before any reminder was raised fails (there is nothing to draw yet).

    orgs Server

    Open the row of an orgs result view

    Command: org_orgs_goto_row Keys: enter (in an orgs result view), double click Args: transient (default false)

    In the result views (Org Habits, Org Clock Report, Org Text Search) each line remembers the file and line it came from; this opens it. A double click on a row does the same. transient opens it as a preview. Not in the command palette: it only means something in those views.

    Org: orgs Attachments

    Command: org_orgs_attachments Keys: none

    Lists the attachments of the heading at the cursor (its attachment folder from :ID: or :DIR:) with type, size and date, and opens the one you pick. The file is downloaded from the server into a new private temporary directory; text, .org, .txt and .md files open in Sublime, anything else in the system's default application. Says why when the heading has no attachment folder. Needs the orgs server.

    Org: orgs Clock Report

    Command: org_orgs_clock_report Keys: none Args: block

    The time clocked across every org file for a range, as a table in the "Org Clock Report" view: each clocked heading (indented by level), its file and its time, with the total. Pick the range from a quick panel or pass block: today, yesterday, thisweek, lastweek, thismonth, lastmonth, thisyear, lastyear, untilnow. enter on a row opens the heading, g refreshes. Needs the orgs server.

    Org: orgs Contacts / Org: orgs Records

    Command: org_orgs_contacts Keys: none Args: query, collection (default "contact")

    Searches the server's records (headings the server reads as contacts, equipment, and other record types) and jumps to the one you pick. Asks for a search text matched against names, numbers, addresses and notes; empty lists them all. Each row shows the first few fields and the file.

    collection picks the record type; "*" (the palette's "Org: orgs Records") first lists the collections with their counts. With query given there is no prompt. Needs the orgs server. Settings: orgsPreviewOnHighlight.

    Org: orgs Decrypt Heading

    Command: org_orgs_decrypt_heading Keys: none Args: write

    Decrypts the heading at the cursor. A quick panel asks whether to show the text (the file stays encrypted) or decrypt into the file (writes the text back in the clear); write true / false answers it in advance. Asks for the passphrase unless the server's gpg is unlocked.

    Shown text goes in an output panel, never a view, so it is not written into Sublime's session; the panel is emptied as soon as it is hidden or the window closes. Needs the orgs server with encryption turned on.

    Org: orgs Delete Saved Query

    Command: org_orgs_delete_query Keys: none Args: name
