    Lists your saved queries, asks for confirmation and deletes the one you pick (or name directly, without asking). Needs the orgs server.

    Org: orgs Drill Flashcards

    Command: org_orgs_drill Keys: none Args: deck, query

    Reviews org-drill style flashcards. Pick one of the server's saved decks or "Query…" (prefilled with orgsDrillQuery); deck or query skip the choice. Due cards (failed, overdue, young, new, old; up to the deck's maximum, 30 by default) are shown one at a time in an "Org Drill" view with clozes ([text] or [text||hint]) hidden; a quick panel offers Show answer, Skip, Open the card or Stop. After the answer you grade it 0-5 and the server schedules the next review (a failed card comes back in the same session). Grading rewrites the card's properties in its file. Needs the orgs server.

    Org: orgs Encrypt Heading

    Command: org_orgs_encrypt_heading Keys: none

    Encrypts the body of the heading at the cursor in the org-crypt format, done by the server's gpg. With a key configured on the server (or the server's gpg already unlocked) it just encrypts; otherwise it asks for a passphrase twice (masked) and checks they match. Needs the orgs server with encryption turned on in its config; otherwise it says encryption is off.

    Org: orgs File History

    Command: org_orgs_file_history Keys: none

    The git history of the current file, from the server: a quick panel lists the working copy (with its uncommitted change counts), the index when something is staged, and up to orgsHistoryLimit commits (subject, author, date, lines added and removed). Picking one opens the file as it was then in a read only scratch view. Needs the orgs server, and the file in a git repository on the server's side.

    Org: orgs Full Text Search

    Command: org_orgs_text_search Keys: none Args: query, in_view (default false), current_file (default false), ignore_case

    A regular expression search over the text of every org file the server has. Asks for the expression (prefilled with the selection, the word at the cursor, or the last search). The matches go in a quick panel (file, line: text, previewed as you move) or, with in_view (palette: "Org: orgs Full Text Search (results view)"), in an "Org Text Search" view laid out like Find Results, where enter or a double click opens a match and g searches again. current_file (palette: "… in This File") searches only the active file. ignore_case overrides orgsTextSearchIgnoreCase. Needs the orgs server.

    Settings: orgsTextSearchMax, orgsTextSearchIgnoreCase, orgsPreviewOnHighlight.

    Org: orgs Habits

    Command: org_orgs_habits Keys: none Args: days

    Opens the "Org Habits" view: every habit (a repeating TODO with :STYLE: habit) with today's state (done, due, LATE), its current and best streak, its completion rate and a bar of the last days days (default orgsHabitDays, 21; the server shows at least 7): ■ done, × missed, · nothing due. enter or a double click opens the habit, t ticks it done for today (Org: orgs Toggle Habit Done Today), g refreshes. Needs the orgs server.

    Org: orgs New File from Template

    Command: org_orgs_new_file Keys: none

    Creates an org file through the server: pick one of the server's org directories (no choice when there is one), type a file name (.org is added), a title, and a server template (or none). The new file is opened. A name that already exists just opens that file. Needs the orgs server.

    Org: orgs Open Web UI

    Command: org_orgs_open_web Keys: none Args: app

    Opens worg, the orgs web ui, in your browser. A quick panel picks the worg app (Agenda, Search, Saved Queries, Kanban, Gantt Chart, Column View, Clock Report, Tables, Files, Links, Mind Map, Collections, Contacts, Code, Flashcards, Diff & History, Presentation, Voice Notes, Starmap); app (e.g. "Kanban") skips it. The url is orgsWebUrl, or the server url when that is empty. When you are logged in (and orgsWebUrl is not set) it opens a one-use login link the server hands out (POST /login/ticket), so the browser is logged in too; it is good once, for a minute, and no token is put on the url. Otherwise worg asks for its own login. Enabled when a server is known or orgsWebUrl is set.

    Org: orgs Query Search

    Command: org_orgs_search Keys: none Args: query, edit (default false)

    Searches every heading the server knows with the orgs query language (e.g. IsTodo() && HasTags("WORK")). Without arguments a quick panel offers "New query…" (an input panel, prefilled with the last query), your saved queries and the server's named filters (run as {{FilterName}}). The matches are listed in a quick panel; picking one opens it at its line. With query the search runs at once; with edit as well it is put in the input panel first.

    Needs the orgs server (disabled when not connected). Settings: orgsPreviewOnHighlight.

    Org: orgs Refresh Result View

    Command: org_orgs_refresh_view Keys: g (in an orgs result view)

    Rebuilds the current orgs result view (habits, clock report, text search results) by running the command that made it again, with the same arguments. Only shown in views that can be refreshed. Needs the orgs server.

    Org: orgs Save Query

    Command: org_orgs_save_query Keys: none Args: query, name

    Saves a query on the server under a name. Saved queries belong to your login and are shared with worg and the orgs command line; they show up in Org: orgs Query Search. Asks for the query (prefilled with the last search) and then the name, unless given as arguments. Needs the orgs server.

    Org: orgs Toggle Habit Done Today

    Command: org_orgs_habit_toggle Keys: t (in an orgs result view)

    In the Org Habits view: marks the habit on the cursor's line done for today (sets its done keyword, so the server advances the repeat and logs it), or, when it is already done today, takes today's tick back. An open, modified buffer of the habit's file is saved first. The view is refreshed afterwards. Only does something in the habits view (in the other result views t just says there is no habit on the line). Needs the orgs server.

    Org: orgs Upcoming Birthdays

    Command: org_orgs_birthdays Keys: none Args: days

    Lists the birthdays and anniversaries from your records in the next days days (default orgsBirthdayDays, 60): date, name, the field, the age they turn when the year is known, and the file. Picking one jumps to the record. Needs the orgs server.

    Org: orgs Update Heading (Jira/plugin)

    Command: org_orgs_update_heading Keys: none Args: name

    Runs a server updater plugin on the heading at the cursor, for example refreshing a heading from its Jira issue. Asks for the plugin name, prefilled with orgsDefaultUpdater ("jira"); name skips the question. The buffer is saved and synced first (orgsSaveBeforeServerEdits) and the server rewrites the heading in the file. Fails with a message when the plugin is not configured on the server. Needs the orgs server.

    Source Blocks

    Org Exec All Source Blocks

    Command: org_execute_all_source_blocks Keys: none Args: amExporting (makes :eval query-export ask), onDone.

    Runs every source block in the buffer, one at a time from the bottom of the file to the top. The html, latex and reveal.js exporters run this first when their execute-on-export setting is on.

    Org Exec Inline Source Block

    Command: org_execute_inline_source_block Keys: alt+o c c (through Org Recalc, on inline code) Args: at, silent, skipSaveWarning, callbacks as for Org Exec Source Block.

    Runs inline code such as src_python[:var x=2]{print(x*2)} at the cursor and puts the result right after it as {{{results(=VALUE=)}}}, replacing an earlier result. Only replace mode is supported.

    Org Exec Source Block

    Command: org_execute_source_block Keys: alt+o c c (through Org Recalc, on a block); vi command mode space c c Args: at (a point in the block, default the cursor), silent, amExporting, skipSaveWarning, and callbacks used by other commands (onDone, onDoneResultsPos, onDoneFnName, onAdjustParams).

    Runs the #+BEGIN_SRC block the cursor is in and writes its output into the #+RESULTS: block under it, creating one when needed. The language must be a source block handler (builtinSourceBlockHandlers, its builtinSourceBlockAliases, or a module in Packages/User/orgsrc/). The org file must exist on disk; unsaved changes are saved first. Header arguments decide what is passed in and how the result is written (see Reference > Source Blocks > Header arguments). Table results are aligned; image-producing languages refresh the inline images.

    Settings: orgBabelDefaultHeaderArgs, babel-args, builtinSourceBlockHandlers, builtinSourceBlockAliases.

    Org Execute Call

    Command: org_execute_call_comment Keys: alt+o c c (through Org Recalc, on a #+CALL: line) Args: onDone (internal callback).

    On an indented #+CALL: name(a=1, b=x) line (the pattern needs whitespace before #+CALL:), runs the source block named name in this file with those values replacing its :var values, and writes the result under the #+CALL: line. The called block's own results are not touched (it is run silently).

    Org Tangle File

    Command: org_tangle_file Keys: none Args: onDone (internal callback).

    Writes the source blocks that have :tangle yes out to files next to the org file: one file per language, named after the org file with the language's extension (notes.org gives notes.sh, notes.js…; python, which has no extension of its own, gives .py). Blocks are appended in file order, each preceded by a comment with its line number; the first block of each file gets a header comment (source file, user, date). Indentation common to the block is removed. Unlike Emacs a :tangle FILENAME is not used as the output name: only yes or no matters.

    Org: orgs Execute Source Block

    Command: org_orgs_babel_exec Keys: none Args: all (default false)

    Runs the source block or #+CALL: line at the cursor on the server and writes its results into the file; with all true (palette: "Org: orgs Execute All Source Blocks") every block in the file. The buffer is saved first and must then match the file on disk exactly; the buffer reloads with the results. The server refuses unless babel.enable is set in its orgs.yaml; that refusal is shown in a dialog. Needs the orgs server.

    Org: orgs Tangle File

    Command: org_orgs_tangle Keys: none Args: write (default true)

    Tangles the current file's source blocks (those with :tangle) on the server, which writes the tangled files; the status bar lists each file and its line count, or says there was nothing to tangle. The buffer is saved and synced first. Needs the orgs server.

    Tables

    Execute every formula of a table

    Command: org_execute_table Keys: alt+o c c (through Org Recalc, in a table) Args: skipFormula, at (a point in the table), clearHighlights (default true), onDone.

    Not in the command palette; Org Recalc runs it when the cursor is in a table. Picks up a new formula typed into the cell at the cursor (see Org Eval Cell), then evaluates every #+TBLFM: formula of the table in order, writing the results cell by cell and re-aligning the table after each one.

    Org Clear Table Cell

    Command: org_clear_cell Keys: vi command mode space t k (in a table) Args: onDone (internal callback).

    Empties the cell under the cursor and re-aligns the table.

    Org Clear Table Highlights

    Command: org_clear_table_regions Keys: none Args: at (a point in the table, default the cursor).

    Removes the formula and cell highlights drawn on a table (the ones that appear as you move through a table or a #+TBLFM: line). Run automatically when the cursor leaves the table.

    Org Convert Region To Table

    Command: org_convert_selection_to_table Keys: none Args: onDone (internal callback).

    Replaces the selected text (more than 6 characters) with an org table. The text is first tried as CSV (python's csv reader); failing that the separator is guessed from the lines: comma, semicolon, tab or space, whichever appears the most consistently per line (comma wins a tie). The table is indented to the level of the heading the cursor is in, then aligned with the Table Editor package.

    Org Edit Table Formula

    Command: org_edit_formula_for_cell Keys: vi command mode space t e (in a table) Args: onDone (internal callback).

    Puts the text of the #+TBLFM: formula that writes the cell under the cursor into that cell, so it can be edited in place. Edit it and run Org Eval Cell (or Org Recalc) to store it back and recompute. Nothing happens when no formula targets the cell.

    Org Eval Cell

    Command: org_fill_in_formula_from_cell Keys: none Args: at, clearHighlights (default true), onDone (when given only the formula is stored; the table is not run).

    Turns what is typed in the cell at the cursor into a #+TBLFM: entry, then runs the table:

    • :=EXPR makes a field formula for this cell (@R$C=EXPR)
    • >=EXPR makes a row formula (@R=EXPR)
    • =EXPR makes a column formula ($C=EXPR)

    An existing formula for the cell is replaced; otherwise the formula is added to the #+TBLFM: line. A cell without one of those prefixes just runs the table.

    Org Execute All Tables

    Command: org_execute_all_tables Keys: none

    Runs every table in the buffer, top to bottom, one after the other, as if Org Recalc had been run in each. Old cell highlights are cleared once at the start.

    Org Execute Formula

    Command: org_execute_formula Keys: none Args: skipFormula, at (a point in the table), clearHighlights (default true), onDone.

    Evaluates only the #+TBLFM: formula that targets the cell under the cursor, writing each value it produces and re-aligning the table after every cell. First, as with Org Eval Cell, a cell that starts with :=, = or >= is turned into a formula (unless skipFormula is true). Values that are floats are formatted by the formula's ;%... format when it has one.

    Org Highlight Formula

    Command: org_highlight_formula Keys: none

    With the cursor on a #+TBLFM: line, highlights the cells written by the formula under the cursor. This runs by itself as the cursor moves along the formula line; the command is there to call it by hand.

    Org Import Csv

    Command: org_import_table_from_csv Keys: none Args: onDone (internal callback).

    Asks for a file path in an input box that completes file names as you type (up and down pick a match), reads the file and inserts it at the cursor as an org table, converted the same way as Org Convert Region To Table (CSV first, otherwise a guessed separator).

    Org Insert Blank Table

    Command: org_insert_blank_table Keys: none Args: onDone (internal callback).

    Asks for the size as WxH (for example 3x4) and inserts an empty table of W columns with a header row, a separator line and H body rows, indented to the current heading, with the cursor in the first cell.

    Org Insert Rnd Table Row

    Command: org_insert_random_row_from_table Keys: none Args: tblName (skip the picker and use this table), onDone.

    Inserts one row, chosen at random, from a named table. Without tblName a quick panel lists the tables: the #+NAME: tables of this file and, when the orgs server is connected, every named table it knows in any org file (a table can also be found through a heading ID). With the server the table is looked up there and the row picked locally; otherwise only this file is searched. Handy for random tables (encounters, prompts, names).

    Uses the orgs server when connected; works on the current file without it.

    Org Output Table Docs

    Command: org_doc_table Keys: none

    With the cursor in a table, appends to the end of the buffer a list of every function a table formula can call, each with its documentation string, then the constant names (pi, t, nil…). Includes functions added by table extensions. Run it in a scratch org file to get the current function reference.

    Org Plot Table

    Command: org_plot_table Keys: none Args: onDone (internal callback).

    Plots the table at the cursor (or the table below a #+PLOT: line when the cursor is on that line) with gnuplot. The #+PLOT: options of the heading are read (see Reference > Tables > #+PLOT options), a data file and a gnuplot script are written next to the org file, gnuplot is run, and both temporary files are deleted. The picture is linked under the table in a #+RESULTS: block (replaced on the next plot) and inline images are cycled so it shows. With file:viewer no file is written and gnuplot's own window opens (on Windows).

    Needs gnuplot: the gnuplot setting is its executable.

    Org Show Table Rows / Org Hide Table Rows

    Commands: org_show_table_rows, org_hide_table_rows Keys: none Args: onDone (internal callback).

    Show Table Rows draws the formula coordinates of the table at the cursor as inline phantoms: the row number (as @N counts it) at the start of each row, roman numerals (I, II…) on the horizontal lines, and the column number ($N) in front of each cell. Hide Table Rows removes every phantom it drew. Nothing in the buffer changes.

    Org Table Exec Below

    Command: org_exec_on_column Keys: none Args: onDone (internal callback).

    Asks for an expression (the right hand side of a formula, as in $1*2) and evaluates it once into every cell of the current column from the cursor's row to the last row. The formula is temporary: it is not kept in #+TBLFM:. A quick way to fill or transform a column.

    Table cursor highlights (internal)

    Commands: org_highlight_cell, org_highlight_formula_from_cell, org_table_auto_compute Keys: none

    Run by the table event listener as the cursor moves: the cell under the cursor is outlined (unless tableShowCursor is false) and the cells of the formula that writes it are highlighted. org_table_auto_compute runs when a Table Editor command is used on an auto-compute row (one whose first cell is #): the table is aligned and the cell at the cursor is recomputed from its formula. Not meant to be bound.

    Settings: tableShowCursor.

    Dynamic Blocks

    clocktable

    #+BEGIN: clocktable :maxlevel 3
#+END:

    A table of the clocked time of the heading the block is in and of every heading below it: a Heading column (sub headings prefixed by \_) and the time spent, each level's time in its own column.

    • :maxlevel N the number of level columns (default 2, minimum 2). All sub headings are listed whatever the value.
    • :scope only subtree (the default) is implemented.

    The table is aligned after it is written. For reports across files use the orgs server's clock report.

    columnview

    #+COLUMNS: %40ITEM(Task) %TODO %10Effort(Estimate) %ALLTAGS
#+BEGIN: columnview :id global :maxdepth 2 :indent t
#+END:

    A table with one row per heading and one column per entry of the #+COLUMNS: line (default %70ITEM(Task) %17Effort(Effort)). A column is %[WIDTH]NAME[(TITLE)]; the width and any {summary} are read but not used. NAME is a property (looked up as written, then upper and lower case) or one of: ITEM (the heading), TODO, PRIORITY, TAGS (the heading's own), ALLTAGS (with inherited), SCHEDULED, DEADLINE, CLOSED, TIMESTAMP (first active timestamp), TIMESTAMP_IA (first inactive one), FILE.

    Parameters:

    • :id which headings: global (default, the whole file), local (the children of the top level heading the block is under), file:NAME (another org file, found through the file database), or an ID / CUSTOM_ID (the children of that heading).
    • :maxdepth N how deep to go (default 0, no limit).
    • :indent t indents ITEM with .. per level.
    • :hlines t a separator before every row; :hlines N before rows down to depth N.
    • :exclude-tags (a b) leaves out headings with those tags.
    • :skip-empty-rows t leaves out rows whose columns are (almost) all empty.

    A block that finds nothing shows |NO COLUMNVIEW DATA|.

    insertdatetime

    #+BEGIN: insertdatetime
#+END:

    Writes the current date and time (python's 2026-10-11 14:03:00.123456 form) into the block. Takes no parameters; a simple example of a dynamic block writer.

    Writing a dynamic block

    A dynamic block writer is a python module in Packages/User/orgdynamic/ (or the bundled orgdynamic/), named as the block:

    • Execute(view, params) (required) returns the block's new lines as a list of strings. params holds the :name value pairs of the #+BEGIN: line (params.Get(name, default), GetInt, GetList).
    • PostExecute(view, params, region) (optional) runs after the text is in the buffer, for example to align a table.

    Exporting

    Html export options

    Org Export File As Html reads, besides the common keywords:

    • #+HTML_STYLE: (setting HtmlStyle, default blocky) the style: blocky, funky, plain, refined ship with OrgEverywhere. A style is STYLE.css plus optional STYLE_inheader.html (added to <head>), STYLE_heading.html (start of <body>) and STYLE_footing.html (end of <body>), looked up in Packages/User/htmlstyles/ first, then in the package's htmlstyles/.
    • Extra css and html, each either inline text (anything with < or {) or the path of a file to include. In the current code the in-file keyword and the setting names are swapped: the keyword is #+HtmlCss: / #+HtmlInHeader: / #+HtmlHeading: / #+HtmlFooting: and the setting is HTML_CSS / HTML_INHEADER / HTML_HEADING / HTML_FOOTING.
    • #+HTML: a line of raw html.
    • #+ATTR_HTML: :caption TEXT captions the next table.
    • <!-- NAME attr"value" … –>= the attributes are added to the next image whose link contains NAME (for example a width).
    • Heading properties become attributes of the heading's <section>.

    Every heading is a collapsible section. Code is highlighted with highlight.js from a CDN (HTML_HIGHLIGHT / HtmlHighlight is read but not used at present). Images are found as for latex (relative to the file, then imageSearchPath, then an images folder of an org directory). A postamble with date, author and creation time ends the page.

    Latex export options

    Org Export File As Latex / As Pdf read, besides the common keywords:

    • #+LATEX_CLASS: (setting latexClass, default article) the document class. Level 1 headings become \section, level 2 \subsection, level 3 \subsubsection, level 4 \paragraph, level 5 and deeper \subparagraph.
    • #+LATEX_CLASS_OPTIONS: appended as is to the end of the \documentclass{CLASS} line (so [a4paper] lands after the class name, which latex rejects).
    • #+LATEX_HEADER: a line added to the preamble.
    • #+LATEX: a line of raw latex; @@...@@ raw latex inside a line.
    • #+OPTIONS: toc:nil (no table of contents), toc:N (its depth), title:nil (no \maketitle), author:nil, date:nil.
    • #+ATTR_LATEX: for the next table or picture: :caption, :float (t, nil, multicolumn, sideways, wrap), :placement (as [h]), :center nil, :width, :height, :scale, :options; tables also :environment (default tabular) and :mode (math, inline-math).
    • $...$, \(...\) and \[...\] math pass through.

    The preamble loads listings, hyperref, graphicx, longtable, wrapfig, rotating, amsmath, amssymb, ulem, enumitem, pifont and a few more. Source blocks use the listings package, with the language mapped by latexListingPackageLang. Links to http become \href, plain names \hyperref, pictures \includegraphics (default width .8\linewidth) with a \graphicspath built from their folders.

    Reveal.js export options

    Org Export File As Reveal Js makes a slide show: each heading is a <section> (a slide), nested under its parent. File keywords, each with a setting used when the keyword is missing:

    • #+REVEAL_THEME: (RevealTheme, default league) black, white, league, beige, sky, night, serif, simple, solarized, moon…
    • #+REVEAL_TRANS: (RevealTransition, default none) none, fade, slide, convex, concave, zoom.
    • #+REVEAL_TRANS_SPEED: (RevealTransitionSpeed, default default) default, fast, slow.
    • #+REVEAL_HIGHLIGHT: (RevealHighlight, default zenburn) the highlight.js theme.
    • #+REVEAL_CSS: (RevealCss) css added inline.
    • #+REVEAL_LOCATION: (RevealLocation, default the reveal.js 4.1.0 CDN) where reveal.js is loaded from.
    • #+REVEAL_VLEVEL: (RevealVLevel) read but not used yet.

    Heading properties set slide backgrounds and transitions: reveal_background / reveal_background_image, reveal_background_size, reveal_background_position, reveal_background_repeat, reveal_background_opacity, reveal_background_color, reveal_background_video, reveal_background_video_loop, reveal_background_video_muted, reveal_background_trans, reveal_trans, reveal_trans_speed.

    #+BEGIN_NOTES blocks become speaker notes. Body text is handled as by the html exporter (#+ATTR_REVEAL: is read for pictures).

    What the built in exporters read

    The html, latex/pdf and reveal.js exporters share one reader. Keywords are case sensitive (write them in upper case). File level options are read from the lines before the first heading, but those lines are not exported themselves: the document is the headings and their text, so line based keywords (#+SETUPFILE:, #+LATEX_HEADER:, #+HTML:…) only take effect inside a heading.

    • #+TITLE:, #+AUTHOR:, #+DATE:, #+EMAIL:, #+LANGUAGE: the document's metadata (html uses title, author and language; latex title, author and date).
    • #+SETUPFILE: path the lines of that file are read in its place.
    • #+CAPTION: captions the next table (latex: also the next picture).
    • #+NAME: becomes an anchor (html) or a \label (latex).
    • <<target>> becomes an anchor or label.
    • #+BEGIN_SRC blocks: with :exports results or none the code is left out. The #+RESULTS: line is dropped but the results under it are always exported, whatever :exports says.
    • Dynamic blocks (#+BEGIN: ...) are exported as preformatted text unless their :exports is results or none.
    • #+BEGIN_QUOTE, #+BEGIN_EXAMPLE, #+BEGIN_NOTES (html: a notes aside), other #+BEGIN_x blocks (preformatted).
    • #+BEGIN_EXPORT LANG blocks are copied through by the matching exporter (http for html and reveal.js, latex for latex).
    • Lists (-=/=+, 1.=/=1), checkboxes, word :: definition), tables, bold, italic, underline, strike, verbatim, code, links.
    • Dropped: drawers, SCHEDULED=/=DEADLINE=/=CLOSED=/=CLOCK lines, #+TBLFM:, #+ATTR_ORG:, #+COLUMNS, #+PRIORITIES, #+PLOT, #+TODO, #+TAGS, #+PROPERTY.

    The output is written next to the org file with the same name.

    Settings

    Agenda

    Agenda layout settings
    Setting Default Effect
    firstDayOfWeek "Sunday" First day of the week view and of the calendar (Monday … Sunday).
    agendaWeekViewNumDays 7 Days in the week view; 5 with firstDayOfWeek Monday shows the work week.
    weekViewDayNames ["Mon","Tue","Wed","Thr","Fri","Sat","Sun"] Day labels of the week view, Monday first.
    agendaDayStartTime 6 First hour of the day and week hour grids.
    agendaDayEndTime 19 Last hour of the grids (at most 23).
    agendaHeaderFormat "%A \t%d %B %Y" strftime format of the date heading of the Day view.
    AgendaCustomViews

    Default:

    {
    "Default": ["Calendar", "Week", "Day", "Blocked Projects", "Next Tasks", "Loose Tasks"],
    "Todos":   ["Todos"],
    "Notes":   ["Notes"],
    "Flags":   ["Todos : tagfilter |TAG1 |OTHERTAGS", "Todos : tagfilter OTHERTAGS"]
}

    The agendas Org Agenda Custom View and Org Agenda Choose View offer: each name maps to a list of views shown one under the other. A view is Name : arg value : flag .... The names: Calendar, Week, Day, Todos, Blocked Projects, Not Blocked Projects, Projects, Next Tasks, Loose Tasks, Done, Clocked, Has Status, Notes, Meetings, Phone, and OrgsQuery (query EXPR, or filter NAME for a server filter, and title TEXT; a query cannot contain a :).

    Filters every view takes: tagfilter, priorityfilter, statefilter (space separated; plain or + must match, | one of, - must not), durationfilter and clockfilter (durations, + before / - after), datefilter (>DATE, >=DATE, <DATE, <=DATE on the closed date, e.g. >=20240101), and the flags hasclock, hasdeadline, hasclose, hasschedule, haschildtasks, noclock, nodeadline, noclose, noschedule, nochildtasks, onlytasks. Todo list views also take byproject, showtotalduration, sortascend / sortdescend, hidefilename, hidestatus, hideheading and column widths showduration, showdate, showtime, showeffort, showafter, showassigned, showid.

    agendaOrgsQueryDefault and agendaSaveBeforeRender
    Setting Default Effect
    agendaOrgsQueryDefault "IsTodo() && !IsArchived()" The query offered by Org: Agenda Query, and run by an OrgsQuery view with no query or filter.
    agendaSaveBeforeRender false Save modified org buffers (and wait for the server to read them) before fetching an agenda.

    The agenda comes from the orgs server, which reads saved files; without agendaSaveBeforeRender an agenda notes how many unsaved org buffers are not in it.

    agendaProjectIs

    Default: "nested_todo"

    What the agenda counts as a project (for Blocked Projects, Next Tasks, Loose Tasks, Projects and byproject): "nested_todo", a todo with todos under it; "tag", a heading tagged :PROJECT:; "property", a heading with a PROJECT property.

    Todo list settings
    Setting Default Effect
    agendaTodoFilterByDefault false Open the filter input (type a regular expression to narrow the list) with todo views.
    agendaTodoSortAscending true Sort order of todo lists; a view's sortascend / sortdescend overrides it.

    refile "" (unset in code) The file captures go to ({refile} in a target) and that Org Open Refile opens.

    Clocking

    Clocking settings
    Setting Default Effect
    clockShowInStatus true Show the running clock ("Clock: heading (h:mm)") in the status bar of org views.
    orgsClockPollSeconds 120 How often (seconds, at least 15) to ask the orgs server for its clock, which it can stop by itself (e.g. its autoclockout plugin). Clock events update it in between.
    clockingSubMinuteClocks true Offline clock only: false removes a clock shorter than a minute on clock out instead of writing it.

    Connection

    Local orgs server settings

    For the server Org: Set Up a Local orgs Server downloads and runs.

    Setting Default Effect
    orgsServerAutoStart true Start the local server when Sublime starts, if it is not already running.
    orgsServerAutoLogin true Log in to the local server as sublimetext with the password Sublime keeps for it, so you are never asked. false asks, like any other server.
    orgsServerCheckForUpdates true Once a day, ask github whether there is a newer orgs release and offer it.

    The server is the local one when orgsUrl is its address (set up writes it). Its files live in your user data folder, not in Packages: on macOS ~/Library/Application Support/OrgEverywhere/orgs, on Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\OrgEverywhere\orgs, on Linux ~/.local/share/OrgEverywhere/orgs.

    orgs live updates and status bar
    Setting Default Effect
    orgsEvents true Listen to the server's change event stream, which keeps the agenda, ids, backlinks and the clock current when files change outside Sublime.
    orgsShowStatus true Show the connection ("orgs: url (user)", "login needed", "connecting…", "offline") in the status bar of org views.
    orgs login settings
    Setting Default Effect
    orgsRememberLogin true Also keep a salted hash of the password (never the password) so an expired session logs back in without asking. Only in a secure store.
    orgsCredentialStore "auto" "auto" uses the OS secret store (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, or secret-tool on Linux) and falls back to a file. "file" forces the file.
    orgsUser not set The user name offered at the login prompt (after the last one used).
    orgsPromptLoginOnStartup true Ask for a login at startup when the server wants one; false waits until a command needs the server.

    The session token (and its user and expiry) is always stored, per server url. The file store is a file only you can read, under Sublime's cache directory (OrgEverywhere/); it is treated as insecure, so the password hash is never put in it. Org: Log out of orgs deletes what is stored.

    orgs server connection

    Settings that decide whether and where OrgEverywhere finds its orgs server.

    Setting Default Effect
    orgsEnabled true false runs without a server: no connection is attempted and the cross file features have no database.
    orgsUrl not set The server url, no trailing slash. When set it is the only url tried.
    orgsDiscoverUrls ["http://localhost:8010", "https://localhost:443"] Tried in order when orgsUrl is not set; the first orgs server that answers wins.
    orgsNoVerify false Turn off https certificate verification (self signed certificates).
    orgsCaFile not set A certificate (e.g. the server's server.crt) to trust for https, instead of turning verification off.
    orgsTimeout 15 Seconds to wait for a server answer, and for the probe of orgsUrl (orgsDiscoverUrls probes wait 2s).
    orgsRetrySeconds 60 When no server is found (or it goes away), look again after this many seconds. 0 never retries.

    A server is recognised by its /salt route, the one route that answers without a login. Org: Set orgs server url writes orgsUrl for you.

    A local server the vscode plugin (Org Everywhere for VS Code) set up is found too: its address is tried after orgsDiscoverUrls, and its own self-signed certificate is trusted for that address only, so neither orgsCaFile nor orgsNoVerify is needed. Log in to it with a user of that server (the plugin's own password stays in VS Code).

    orgsPathMap

    Default: {}

    For a server on another machine or in a container, whose file paths differ from yours: a map from the server's path prefixes to the local prefixes holding the same files, e.g. { "/home/me/org": "~/Dropbox/org" }. The longest matching prefix wins; ~ is expanded on the local side. A server on this machine needs no map.

    orgsPreviewOnHighlight

    Default: true

    Quick panels that list headings from the server (query search, agenda query, contacts, birthdays, text search…) open the highlighted heading in a transient preview as you move through the list. false only jumps when you pick one.

    orgsSaveBeforeServerEdits

    Default: true

    Commands that have the server edit a file (refile, copy, archive, agenda actions, clocking, updater plugins, exports that rewrite the file…) first make the server see the buffer: a modified buffer of the file is saved and OrgEverywhere waits for the server to re-read it. With false such a command refuses ("save the file first") instead of saving for you.

    Day Pages

    Day page settings

    With the orgs server these apply only when the server has no dayPagePath of its own (dayPageCopyTasksForToday and dayPageNameFormat, to recognise a page, apply always).

    Setting Default Effect
    dayPagePath not set Folder of the day pages (a string; created if missing). Not set: no local day pages.
    dayPageNameFormat "%a_%Y_%m_%d" strftime name of a page (without .org). Old pages are found by this name, so do not change it lightly.
    dayPageSnippet "dayPageSnippet" The snippet (in orgsnippets, without .sublime-snippet) a new page is filled from.
    dayPageMode "day" "week" makes one page per week.
    dayPageModeWeekDay "Monday" In week mode, the day whose date names the week's page.
    dayPageArchiveOld true Tag the previous page #+FILETAGS: ARCHIVE when a new page is made.
    dayPageCopyOpenTasks true Copy the previous page's top level open todos to a new page.
    dayPageCopyTasksForToday true Copy today's open tasks from other files (from the orgs agenda) to a new page.
    dayPageCreateOldPages false Org Day Page Previous creates the previous day's page instead of skipping to an existing one.

    The day page snippet gets ORG_INACTIVE_DATE, ORG_ACTIVE_DATE, ORG_DATE, ORG_TIME, ORG_CLIPBOARD, ORG_SELECTION, ORG_LINENUM, ORG_FILENAME (the page's name) and ORG_AUTHOR. {daypage} in a capture target is today's page.

    Todo states, priorities and logDone
    • todoStates: the todo keywords of files without #+TODO:. Entries after the "|" entry are done states. Default: ["TODO", "NEXT", "BLOCKED", "WAITING", "FLAG", "CLEANUP", "IN-PROGRESS", "DOING", "|", "CANCELLED", "REASSIGNED", "DONE", "MEETING", "PHONE", "NOTE", "FIXED"].

    Folding

    onFocusRespectStartupFolds

    Default: not set (off).

    When true, each time an org view gets focus and its startup is overview, fold or content, everything except the path to the heading at the cursor is folded again (as Org Fold Others). Links are re-folded on focus either way when it is on.

    startup

    Default: ["showall", "noinlineimages"] in the settings file (code default ["showall"]).

    How files open when they have no #+STARTUP: line of their own (a #+STARTUP: line replaces this list). overview or fold folds every heading; content folds each heading's text; anything else (showall, nofold, showeverything) shows all with drawers folded. Links are folded in every case. The list also carries the other startup words (inlineimages / noinlineimages, logdone, lognotedone) read elsewhere.

    Links

    backlinksUpdate (on focus)

    Default: true.

    When an org file's view gets focus, its backlinks display is refreshed (UpdateBacklinksForDisplay). Set to false to skip that refresh, for example when focus changes feel slow.

    file_exclude_patterns and folder_exclude_patterns

    Default: file_exclude_patterns [".pdf", ".doc", ".docx", ".docm"]; folder_exclude_patterns not set.

    A file: link to a file whose name matches file_exclude_patterns (or whose name is in folder_exclude_patterns) is opened with the system's application instead of in Sublime, unless it matches resolver.local_file.force_into_sublime. Everything else opens in Sublime, at the row, column or heading the link names.

    Link and image settings
    Setting Default Effect
    imageSearchPath [] Folders inline images are looked for in (after the file's own folder).
    linkFindUseRoamTags true Org Link To File shows each file's #+ROAM_TAGS: in the list.
    insertRoamTagToFileLink true Org Link To File puts the roam tags in the link description too; false uses the bare title.
    backlinksUpdate true Keep the Backlinks view current when files are saved or re-read by the server.
    startup ["showall", "noinlineimages"] Global #+STARTUP:; inlineimages shows images when a file opens (folding values are read elsewhere).
    Link resolver settings

    linkResolvers (default ["internal", "http", "https", "prompt", "jira", "email", "file"]) is the order Org Open Link tries its local resolvers in; a resolver module of your own in Packages/User/orgresolver can be named here too. Each resolver reads its own settings:

    • resolver.abstract.commands: the opener command per platform (darwin, win32, linux); default open, cmd /C start, xdg-open. Setting it replaces the default of every resolver, the prompt resolver's terminal command included.
    • resolver.abstract.arg_list_wrapper (default []): a command the opener command line is wrapped in.
    • resolver.http.pattern / resolver.http.url (default ^(http):(?P<url>.+)$ and http:%s), and the same for https: what such a link is and the url opened.
    • resolver.jira.pattern (default ^(jira|j):(?P<issue>.+)$, group issue) and resolver.jira.url (default http://sandbox.onjira.com/browse/%s). While the url is that placeholder, jira links go to the orgs server first.
    • resolver.email.pattern / resolver.email.url (default mailto:%s): mailto: links.
    • resolver.prompt.pattern (default ^(cmd:|prompt:)(?P<path>.+)$) and resolver.prompt.path (default %s, on Linux --working-directory=%s): links that open a terminal in a folder.
    • resolver.local_file.pattern: how a file link splits into the path and its :: search (default in orgresolver/file.py). The internal resolver reads the same key with a different default, so setting it changes both.
    • resolver.local_file.force_into_sublime: file patterns always opened in Sublime even when file_exclude_patterns matches (default text, code and image extensions). A list, or a comma separated string with no quotes or spaces around the patterns.

    default false. Re-import the user extensions every time they are looked up (for developing one). Without it a user module is re-imported only when its file changed; table extensions only once per session.
    forceLoadInternalExtensions

    The orgs server's orgDirs decide which files are org files; OrgEverywhere no longer scans folders itself (orgFiles, orgExcludeDirs and orgExcludeFiles are not read at all). orgDirs is only used when no server is connected, as the org directories whose images folders inline images and exports look in. ~ is expanded; a single string is accepted.

    timesheetPath
    no default. The folder the gantt charts are written to (created when missing); required by both gantt commands.
    mermaidPath

    timesheetDefaultSection

    the start of undated tasks; when unset the code uses 2023-01-02 for the mermaid chart and 2021-05-18 for the Google one.

    A board id list used for files with no #+TRELLO: line by Org Trello Sync Board (which is currently broken from org files, see there).

    Values that refer to other values

    Every string setting (and each string in a list setting) is expanded as a template when read: {date} today (2026-10-11), {time} the time (14:03:00), {datetime} (2026-10-11 Sun 14:03), and {NAME} the value of another setting. OrgEverywhere.sublime-settings is read from Packages/User/ over the package's defaults; on first start a copy of the defaults is put there.

    Notifications

    Notification settings

    OrgEverywhere starts a notification thread a second after it loads. It asks the orgs server for today's agenda (rebuilt every fourth check, on a new day, when the server re-reads a file and when it connects) and raises a reminder for each timed entry that is not done, once, from the lead time before it starts until it starts. A reminder runs the external notification command and shows the Notifications view. Without the server nothing is scheduled.

    Setting Default Effect
    notifyHoursBefore 0 Lead time, hours part.
    notifyMinsBefore 15 Lead time, minutes part (the window is at least 1.5 check periods long).
    noticePeriod 1 Minutes between checks (at least 1). Read when the thread starts.
    ExternalNotificationCommand per OS The command line (a list) run for a reminder; {todo} and {time} are filled in.

    The default command is osascript -e 'display notification ...' on macOS and PowerShell with balloontip.ps1 (from the package folder) on Windows. Linux has no default: set ExternalNotificationCommand there, or the reminder fails.

    orgsWebUrl "" The worg web ui url for Org: orgs Open Web UI; empty uses the server url.
    orgsDefaultUpdater "jira" The updater plugin offered by Org: orgs Update Heading.
    orgsDrillQuery HasTags("drill") The query offered for flashcards when no deck is chosen.

    Setting Default Effect

    Language program paths

    Where the source block languages find their programs. Defaults are the code's (Windows paths); set them for your system.

    /bin/bash (Windows: C:\Windows\System32\wsl.exe). sh / bash blocks.

    Source block languages and default header arguments
    builtinSourceBlockHandlers
    default =["plantuml", "graphviz", "ditaa", "mermaid", "powershell", "python", "gnuplot", "cmd", "sh", "javascript", "perl", "csharp"]=. The bundled languages that may run. Every .py file in Packages/User/orgsrc/ is added as a language too, named after the file.
    builtinSourceBlockAliases
    default {"bash": "sh", "bat": "cmd", "js": "javascript"}. Other names for a language on the #+BEGIN_SRC line.
    orgBabelDefaultHeaderArgs
    default ":session none :results replace :exports default :cache no :noweb no". The header arguments every block starts from.
    babel-args

    babel-args-LANGUAGE
    not set by default. As babel-args for one language, for example babel-args-python.

    Tables

    enableTableExtensions

    Default: not set (off).

    When true, every python file in Packages/User/orgtable/ is loaded as a table extension. A module with an Execute function adds a formula function named after the file; a module with AddSymbols(names) can add constants to the dictionary it is given. Extensions are loaded once per Sublime session unless forceLoadExternalExtensions is true.

    tableShowCursor

    Default: true.

    Outlines the cell under the cursor while moving through a table (the org_highlight_cell listener). Set to false to stop the outline; the formula highlights still show.

    Source Blocks

    Header arguments and where they come from

    The header arguments of a block are merged in this order, later ones replacing earlier ones:

    1. the orgBabelDefaultHeaderArgs setting;
    2. the babel-args setting, then babel-args-LANGUAGE;
    3. #+PROPERTY: header-args: ... and #+PROPERTY: header-args:LANGUAGE: ... lines in the file;
    4. the heading's header-args and header-args:LANGUAGE properties, and a var property;
    5. the nearest #+HEADER: line above the block, within its heading;
    6. the arguments on the #+BEGIN_SRC line itself.

    Arguments OrgEverywhere acts on:

    • :results collection output / value; type table, vector, list, scalar, verbatim, file; format code, drawer, html, latex, org, raw…; handling replace (default), append, prepend, silent (the result is only printed to the console).
    • :exports code, results, both, none, default (used by the exporters).
    • :var name=value a number, a string, or the #+NAME: of a table, a list or another source block in this file (that block is run first and its result passed in).
    • :file name the result is a link to this file (diagram languages write their picture there).
    • :cache yes the block's text is hashed into #+RESULTS[hash]: and the block is not run again while the hash matches.
    • :noweb yes <<name>> and <<name(args)>> lines are replaced by the named blocks' results before running.
    • :eval never / no never run; query asks first; query-export asks only while exporting (never-export and no-export are accepted but not acted on).
    • :tangle yes include the block in Org Tangle File.

    Source Languages

    Adding a language

    Any NAME.py in Packages/User/orgsrc/ becomes the language NAME for source blocks (reloaded when the file changes). The module provides:

    • Execute(cmd, sets) (required) runs the block and returns a list of output lines. cmd.source is the block text, cmd.params the header arguments, cmd.filename the temporary file when Extension exists.
    • Extension(cmd) the file extension; when present the block is written to a temporary file first (and tangles to that extension).
    • PreProcessSourceFile(cmd) rewrite cmd.source before running, for example to define the :var values.
    • WrapStart(cmd) / WrapEnd(cmd) text put around the block.
    • LineCommentPrefix() the comment prefix used when tangling.
    • PostExecute(cmd) runs after the result is in the buffer.
    • GeneratesImages(cmd) return true to refresh inline images after.

    The bundled languages in orgsrc/ are examples.

    beancount (not working)

    Language: beancount (not in the default builtinSourceBlockHandlers)

    Meant to run a beancount block with beancountPath. The handler is unfinished: it is a copy of the javascript one and fails when run (it calls an undefined program path). Leave it out of builtinSourceBlockHandlers.

    cmd (Windows batch)

    Language: cmd, alias bat Tangles to: .bat

    Windows only: runs the block as a .bat file with C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe /Q /C (the path is fixed, not a setting). :var values become set variables; a table becomes NAME[r,c] variables plus NAME_width and NAME_height; a list sets NAME_len. With :results value the block runs as a batch subroutine and the value it leaves in orgEverywhereWrapperVar is the result.

    csharp (experimental)

    Language: csharp Tangles to: .cs

    Writes the block to a temporary .cs file and runs dotnetPath FILE.cs (default C:\Program Files\dotnet\dotnet.exe). The plain dotnet command does not run a loose .cs file, so this needs a dotnet that can (a script runner) to give useful output. :var values become var declarations.

    Settings: dotnetPath.

    ditaa

    Language: ditaa Tangles to: .ditaa

    Runs JAVA -jar DITAA.jar FILE -o on the block and copies the png to :file (default diagram.png) next to the org file. The result is a link to the picture; ditaa's output is shown only when it reports an error.

    Settings: ditaa (the jar, required), java (default java).

    gnuplot

    Language: gnuplot Tangles to: .gplt

    Runs the block with gnuplot (gnuplot setting, default C:\Program Files\gnuplot\bin\gnuplot.exe). With :file name.png the terminal is chosen from the extension (png, jpeg, gif, svg, postscript, canvas for .html, dumb for .txt), set output is added, and the picture is moved next to the org file. A :var data=TABLE table becomes a gnuplot data block $data (tab separated, org dates converted to YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM).

    Settings: gnuplot.

    graphviz

    Language: graphviz Tangles to: .dot

    Runs the graphviz graphviz executable (no default; usually the path of dot) as EXE -TFORMAT FILE -o OUTPUT. Header arguments: :fmt the output format (default png), :file the output file relative to the org file (default diagram.FORMAT), :engine another layout program found next to the executable (neato, circo…). The result is a link to the picture.

    Settings: graphviz.

    javascript

    Language: javascript, alias js Tangles to: .js

    Runs the block as a .js file with node.js (nodejsPath, default C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe; set it on macOS and Linux). :var tables and lists become arrays, numbers and strings let variables. With :results value the block is wrapped in a function and its return value is the result.

    Settings: nodejsPath.

    mermaid

    Language: mermaid Tangles to: .mmd

    Runs the mermaid command line tool, MMDC -i FILE -o OUTPUT (through powershell on Windows), writing :file (default diagram.png) relative to the org file. The result is a link to the picture.

    Settings: mermaid (the path of mmdc; install it with npm install @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli).

    perl

    Language: perl Tangles to: .pl

    Runs the block as a .pl file with perlPath (default C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin\perl.exe; set it on macOS and Linux). :var tables and lists become @name arrays, numbers and strings $name scalars. With :results value the block is wrapped in a sub and its return value is the result.

    Settings: perlPath.

    plantuml

    Language: plantuml Tangles to: .pu

    Wraps the block in @startuml / @enduml, runs java -jar PLANTUML.jar on it and copies the png to :file (default diagram.png), relative to the org file, making the folder when needed. The result is a link to the picture and inline images are refreshed. Needs java on the PATH and the plantuml setting (the jar file; there is no default).

    Settings: plantuml.

    powershell

    Language: powershell Tangles to: .ps1

    Windows only: runs the block as a .ps1 file with the 32 bit Windows PowerShell at a fixed path (C:\Windows\SysWOW64\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe, -ExecutionPolicy Unrestricted). :var tables become arrays of arrays (@(...)), lists arrays, numbers and strings variables. With :results value the block runs as a function and its output value is the result.

    python

    Language: python Tangles to: .py

    Runs the block inside Sublime Text's own python (3.8), not an external interpreter: what it prints is the output. view and window are predefined (the active view and window), so a block can script the editor. :var tables and lists arrive as python lists of lists / lists, numbers as numbers, strings as strings. With :results value the block is wrapped in a function and its return value is the result. No setting is needed. When the block raises, the exception's type and message are added to the output.

    sh (bash)

    Language: sh, alias bash Tangles to: .sh

    Writes the block to a temporary .sh file and runs it with bashPath (default /bin/bash; on Windows C:\Windows\System32\wsl.exe, with the file path rewritten to /mnt/c/...). Runs in Packages/User. :var numbers and strings become shell variables, lists become arrays, tables become a tab separated here-document string. With :results value the block runs as a function and its exit status is the result.

    Settings: bashPath.

    Tables

    #+PLOT options

    Org Plot Table reads the first #+PLOT: line of the heading the table is in. Options are name:value pairs separated by spaces:

    • title: the plot title (default "Table Data").
    • file: the picture to write, relative to the org file or absolute (default plot_YEAR_MONTH_DAY_H_M_S.png next to the org file). The extension picks the gnuplot terminal: .png, .jpg=/.jpeg=, .gif, .svg, .ps, .html (canvas), .txt (dumb). file:viewer opens gnuplot's window instead of writing a file.
    • ind: the column used for the x axis (default 1).
    • deps: the columns to plot, as (2 3 4) (default every column).
    • with: the gnuplot style: lines, points, histograms, candlesticks (four columns per series)… One series per deps column, titled by the column's header cell.
    • using: a raw gnuplot using clause, used when with is not given.
    • set: / unset: a gnuplot set=/=unset line (may repeat).
    • include:header keeps the header row as data instead of commenting it out.
    #+PLOT: title:"Sales" ind:1 deps:(2 3) with:lines file:sales.png

    Settings: gnuplot (the gnuplot executable).

    Formula references follow table edits

    When rows and columns are moved, inserted or deleted with the Table Editor commands (alt+up=/=alt+down move a row, alt+left=/=alt+right move a column, alt+shift+down inserts a row, alt+shift+up kills one, alt+shift+right inserts a column, alt+shift+left deletes one), the @N and $N numbers in the table's #+TBLFM: line are renumbered to match, so formulas keep pointing at the same cells. Row moves at the first row or next to a horizontal line are left alone.

    Table formula functions

    Formulas in #+TBLFM: are python-like expressions (evaluated by a safe evaluator, not python itself). References: $N a column, @N a row, @R$C a cell, @>=/=@< the last/first row, @+1=/=@-1 relative rows, @#=/=$# the current row/column, and ranges with ... Besides python's operators these functions are available:

    Ranges
    vsum, vmean, vmedian, vmax, vmin, vsumifeq(a,b,range), vsumifgt, vsumiflt, vsumifgteq, vsumiflteq (sum the range where the condition between a and b holds for that row).
    Math
    abs, sqrt, pow, exp, log, log10, log2, floor, ceil, round, trunc, sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, sinh, cosh, tanh, asinh, acosh, atanh, degrees, radians, int, float, bool.
    Random
    random(start,end) an integer in the range, randomf() a float from 0 to 1.
    Dates
    now(), date(x), duration(x) (org duration, as 1d 3h), year, month, day, hour, minute, second, time, weekday (Monday is 0), yearday.
    Other tables
    remote(name-or-id, cellRef) a cell of another table, found by #+NAME: in this file or by the ID/CUSTOM_ID of the heading that holds it.
    Colour
    highlight(cell,color,text) colours a cell (green, red, orange, white, black, purple, yellow, cyan) and returns text; red($x), green, yellow, blue, cyan, purple, orange, pink are shortcuts; gradient(cell, progress, colors...) picks a colour by a 1..100 progress value.
    Files
    filename(x) turns a relative file name or link into an absolute path.
    Source blocks
    sbe('name', var=value...) runs the source block with that #+NAME: in this file, its keyword arguments becoming the block's :var values, and fills the cell with its result.
    Tests
    passed(test) writes PASSED (green) or FAILED (red).

    Constants: pi, t=/=true=/=True, nil=/=None, false=/=False. Org Output Table Docs writes the current list with each function's own description. Table extensions (see enableTableExtensions) add more.

    A row whose first cell is # is an auto-compute row: using a Table Editor command on it recomputes the cell at the cursor.
